descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a problem and what I want to happen, but I need help thinking about limits like time or materials. Example: I want to make a bridge that holds weight but forget I only have straws and tape.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what I want to make, but I don’t think about what I’ll need or how it should work. Example: I say I want to build a tower but don’t think about how tall it should be or what materials I can use.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.A Defining Engineering Problems)
text: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or a want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can describe the problem and include limits like cost, time, safety, and materials in detail. Example: “We need a slide for 10 kids at once, under $500, safe in hot weather, and quick to build.”
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can define a design problem with clear limits (what it needs to do and what makes it hard). Example: “We need a new slide that is safe, can fit many kids, and is not too expensive.”
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a problem and one part of what makes it hard to solve, but I don’t explain all the needs. Example: “The slide is too short” but not thinking about making it safe or fun.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what the problem is but not explain clearly what needs to be fixed or improved. Example: “The playground is broken” but not saying which part or why it’s a problem.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions)
text: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare real-life solutions to a problem and explain which one works best and why, based on goals and limits. Example: I evaluate several shelter designs and explain which one keeps animals safe while using the fewest resources.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can think of different ways to solve a problem and compare them to see which one meets the criteria and limits best. Example: I compare two boat designs to decide which one floats better and uses fewer materials.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can share a few ideas to solve a problem, but I need help comparing them or checking if they meet all the requirements. Example: I give two ideas for a tower but don’t explain which one is better for staying under budget.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can come up with one idea to solve a problem, but I don’t think about how well it works or follow the rules. Example: I suggest building a paper bridge but don’t check if it can hold weight or fits the materials limit.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions)
text: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare real-life solutions to a problem and explain which one works best and why, based on goals and limits. Example: I evaluate several shelter designs and explain which one keeps animals safe while using the fewest resources.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can think of different ways to solve a problem and compare them to see which one meets the criteria and limits best. Example: I compare two boat designs to decide which one floats better and uses fewer materials.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can share a few ideas to solve a problem, but I need help comparing them or checking if they meet all the requirements. Example: I give two ideas for a tower but don’t explain which one is better for staying under budget.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can come up with one idea to solve a problem, but I don’t think about how well it works or follow the rules. Example: I suggest building a paper bridge but don’t check if it can hold weight or fits the materials limit.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions)
text: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can make and compare several detailed solutions, explaining which is best with evidence. Example: “We could add two slides, or one spiral slide. Two slides are cheaper and safer, but the spiral slide saves space. Two slides are the best solution.”
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can think of two or more ideas and compare them based on what is most important. Example: “We could make the slide longer or add two slides. Adding two slides is better because it lets more kids play.”
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give more than one idea but only explain why one might work. Example: “We could make the slide longer or add two slides, but I only talk about the longer one.”
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can think of one idea but not more, or I don’t compare it to other ideas. Example: “Make a longer slide.”

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions, ETS1.C Optimizing the Design Solution)
text: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design fair, repeated tests and explain how the results show what parts of my design should be improved or redesigned. Example: I test different parachutes by keeping the drop height the same and use results to improve the parachute’s shape and size.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and do a fair test by changing one thing at a time and use the results to decide what needs to be improved. Example: I test two car ramps by only changing the slope and find out which one makes the car go faster.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can do a test and notice if something doesn’t work, but I need help keeping it fair or finding what to fix. Example: I see that my tower falls over, but I’m not sure which part caused the problem.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can test my idea, but I don’t control the variables or look for what went wrong. Example: I test my paper airplane but don’t fly it the same way each time or check why it didn’t fly far.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions, ETS1.C Optimizing the Design Solution)
text: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design fair, repeated tests and explain how the results show what parts of my design should be improved or redesigned. Example: I test different parachutes by keeping the drop height the same and use results to improve the parachute’s shape and size.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and do a fair test by changing one thing at a time and use the results to decide what needs to be improved. Example: I test two car ramps by only changing the slope and find out which one makes the car go faster.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can do a test and notice if something doesn’t work, but I need help keeping it fair or finding what to fix. Example: I see that my tower falls over, but I’m not sure which part caused the problem.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can test my idea, but I don’t control the variables or look for what went wrong. Example: I test my paper airplane but don’t fly it the same way each time or check why it didn’t fly far.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions, ETS1.C Optimizing the Design Solution)
text: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design detailed tests, collect data, and suggest improvements based on results. Example: “We test the slide with 10 kids. It took too long to wait, so we add another slide to reduce waiting time.”
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and carry out a test, measuring how well it works. Example: “Test if 10 kids can use the slide safely without waiting too long.”
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can suggest a test but don’t say what to measure or how to know if it works. Example: “Let’s see if the slide is fun.”
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say “try it out” but not explain how to test if it works. Example: “We should build it and see.”

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter)
text: Develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules and extended structures.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build models of different molecules and extended structures and explain how the arrangement of atoms is linked to a property of the substance.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop models to show the atoms that make up simple molecules and extended structures.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a given model or kit to show how atoms join to make a simple molecule, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that all matter is made of tiny particles called atoms, using a picture or model.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter, PS1.B Chemical Reactions)
text: Analyze and interpret data on the properties of substances before and after the substances interact to determine if a chemical reaction has occurred.
ee_text: Target Level: Interpret and analyze data on the properties (e.g., color, texture, odor, and state of matter) of substances before and after chemical changes have occurred (e.g., burning sugar or burning steel wool, rust, effervescent tablets). Precursor Level: Gather data on the properties (e.g., color, texture, odor, and state of matter) of substances before and after chemical changes have occurred (e.g., burning sugar or burning steel wool, rust, effervescent tablets). Initial Level: Observe and identify examples of change (e.g. state of matter, color, temperature, and odor).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design a test to collect property data before and after substances mix and use the data to justify whether a chemical reaction happened.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze data on properties of substances before and after they interact to decide if a chemical reaction has occurred.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare one or two properties, like color or smell, before and after mixing, using a data table and sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some signs of a chemical change, such as bubbles, color change, or heat, with picture support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use data on color, texture, smell, or state to tell if a chemical change happened.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter, PS1.B Chemical Reactions)
text: Gather and make sense of information to describe that synthetic materials come from natural resources and impact society.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how a synthetic material made from a natural resource benefits and harms society and suggest a way to reduce the harm.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can gather information to describe how synthetic materials come from natural resources and how they impact society.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can match a synthetic material, like plastic, to the natural resource it comes from, using a text with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort materials into natural and human-made, using pictures and a word bank.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter)
text: Develop a model that predicts and describes changes in particle motion, temperature, and state of a pure substance when thermal energy is added or removed.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a particle model to predict and explain changes in temperature and state for a new substance, such as wax or chocolate, when heat is added or removed.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model that predicts and describes how particle motion, temperature, and state change when thermal energy is added or removed.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw particles in a solid, liquid, and gas and say how they move faster when heated, with a model to guide me.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name solids, liquids, and gases and say that heating can melt or boil a substance, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.B Chemical Reactions)
text: Develop and use a model to describe how the total number of atoms does not change in a chemical reaction and thus mass is conserved.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model and real mass data to explain why mass seems to change in an open container but stays the same in a closed one.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to show that atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, in a chemical reaction, so mass is conserved.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can count atoms on each side of a simple reaction model and say if they match, with step-by-step support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that matter is made of atoms and that atoms can join in new ways, using models or drawings.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.B Chemical Reactions)
text: Undertake a design project to construct, test, and modify a device that either releases or absorbs thermal energy by chemical processes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can test and improve my device several times, using data to explain how changing the amount or type of chemical changes the energy released or absorbed.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can design, build, test, and modify a device that releases or absorbs thermal energy through a chemical process.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can follow a plan to build a hot or cold pack and record its temperature change, with help to improve it.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that some mixtures get hot or cold when they react, using a thermometer with support.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.A Forces and Motion)
text: Apply Newton’s Third Law to design a solution to a problem involving the motion of two colliding objects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design and test a solution for a collision problem and use Newton's Third Law to explain why my design protects the objects better than others.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can apply Newton's Third Law to design a solution to a problem involving two colliding objects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe that when two objects collide they push on each other with equal and opposite forces, using a diagram and frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can show with my hands or objects that a push in one direction causes a push back, with teacher support.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.A Forces and Motion)
text: Plan an investigation to provide evidence that the change in an object’s motion depends on the sum of the forces on the object and the mass of the object.
ee_text: Target Level: Investigate and predict the change in motion of objects based on the forces acting on those objects. Precursor Level: Investigate and identify ways to change the motion of an object (e.g., change an incline's slope to make an object go slower, faster, farther). Initial Level: Identify ways to change the movement of an object (e.g., faster, slower, stop).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can plan a fair test that changes force or mass, collect data, and use it to predict the motion of a new object.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan an investigation to show that an object's change in motion depends on the total forces on it and its mass.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can follow an investigation plan and describe how a bigger push or a heavier object changes motion, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that a push or pull can start, stop, or change the direction of an object, using real objects.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can investigate and predict how an object's motion will change based on the forces acting on it.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.B Types of Interactions)
text: Ask questions about data to determine the factors that affect the strength of electric and magnetic forces.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask testable questions about electric and magnetic forces, analyze data, and design a device, such as a stronger electromagnet, based on my findings.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask questions about data to find the factors that affect the strength of electric and magnetic forces.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask a simple question about magnets or static electricity and read a data table to answer it, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can observe that magnets attract some objects and that charged objects can attract paper, with support.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.B Types of Interactions)
text: Construct and present arguments using evidence to support the claim that gravitational interactions are attractive and depend on the masses of interacting objects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use data from simulations to argue how both mass and distance affect gravitational force and apply this to orbits in the solar system.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct and present an argument with evidence that gravitational forces are attractive and depend on the masses of the objects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain that gravity pulls objects toward each other and that bigger masses pull more, using a chart and sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that gravity pulls things down toward Earth, using a demonstration or picture.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.B Types of Interactions)
text: Conduct an investigation and evaluate the experimental design to provide evidence that fields exist between objects exerting forces on each other even though the objects are not in contact.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design and critique an investigation that maps a field and explain how the evidence shows forces act without contact.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can conduct an investigation and evaluate its design to show that fields exist between objects that exert forces without touching.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can carry out a guided investigation with magnets and describe that they push or pull without touching, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can observe that a magnet can move a paperclip without touching it, with teacher guidance.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.A Definitions of Energy)
text: Construct and interpret graphical displays of data to describe the relationships of kinetic energy to the mass of an object and to the speed of an object.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use graphs to compare how doubling mass and doubling speed affect kinetic energy and explain which change has the bigger effect.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct and interpret graphs of data to describe how kinetic energy relates to an object's mass and to its speed.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a simple graph and say that faster or heavier objects have more motion energy, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that moving objects have energy and that faster objects have more, using real examples.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.A Definitions of Energy, PS3.C Relationship Between Energy and Forces)
text: Develop a model to describe that when the arrangement of objects interacting at a distance changes, different amounts of potential energy are stored in the system.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to compare potential energy stored in gravitational, magnetic, and electric systems and predict what happens when distances change.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to describe that changing the distance between interacting objects changes the potential energy stored in the system.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram to show that lifting an object higher stores more energy, with guided support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that a raised object or stretched spring has stored energy, using a demonstration.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.A Definitions of Energy, PS3.B Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer)
text: Apply scientific principles to design, construct, and test a device that either minimizes or maximizes thermal energy transfer.
ee_text: Target Level: Test and refine a device (e.g., foam cup, insulated box, or thermos) to either minimize or maximize thermal energy transfer (e.g., keeping liquids hot or cold, preventing liquids from freezing, keeping hands warm in cold temperatures). Precursor Level: Investigate objects/materials, and predict their ability to maximize or minimize thermal energy transfer. Initial Level: Identify objects/materials used to minimize or maximize thermal energy transfer (e.g., gloves, vacuum flask, insulated hot pad holder or foam cup).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can test and redesign my device using temperature data and explain how each material choice reduces or increases heat transfer.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can apply science ideas to design, build, and test a device that minimizes or maximizes thermal energy transfer.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can choose materials to keep something hot or cold and test my device with a thermometer, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort materials that keep things warm or cool, such as foam and metal, with picture support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can test and improve a device, such as an insulated cup, that keeps something hot or cold.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.A Definitions of Energy, PS3.B Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer)
text: Plan an investigation to determine the relationships among the energy transferred, the type of matter, the mass, and the change in the average kinetic energy of the particles as measured by the temperature of the sample.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can plan and carry out an investigation, control variables, and use my results to predict temperature changes for different materials and masses.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan an investigation to find how energy transferred, type of matter, mass, and temperature change are related.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can follow a plan to heat or cool water samples and record temperature changes in a table, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use a thermometer to read the temperature of hot and cold water, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.B Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer)
text: Construct, use, and present arguments to support the claim that when the kinetic energy of an object changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use an energy diagram and data to argue where energy goes in a real event, such as a car braking, and account for all of it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct and present an argument that when an object's kinetic energy changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how energy moves when a ball speeds up or slows down, using a diagram and sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that energy can move from one object to another, like when a ball hits another ball.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.A Wave Properties)
text: Use mathematical representations to describe a simple model for waves that includes how the amplitude of a wave is related to the energy in a wave.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use math to compare two waves and explain how changing amplitude changes the energy, using an example such as sound volume.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to describe a wave model and show how amplitude is related to the energy in a wave.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label amplitude and wavelength on a wave diagram and say that bigger waves carry more energy, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can draw a wave and point to its top and bottom, using a model.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.A Wave Properties, PS4.B Electromagnetic Radiation)
text: Develop and use a model to describe that waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through various materials.
ee_text: Target Level: Use a model to show how light waves (e.g., light through a water glass, light on colored objects) or sound waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through various materials (e.g., water, air, table). Precursor Level: Investigate changes in vibrations and sources of sound in everyday life. Initial Level: Use a model to recognize that sound waves are transmitted by vibrations.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to predict and explain how light or sound will behave when it meets a new material, such as glass, water, or foam.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to describe how waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through different materials.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort materials by whether light passes through, bounces off, or is absorbed, using a diagram with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can observe that light bounces off a mirror and passes through clear materials, with teacher support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a model to show how light or sound is reflected, absorbed, or passes through different materials.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.C Information Technologies and)
text: Integrate qualitative scientific and technical information to support the claim that digitized signals are a more reliable way to encode and transmit information than analog signals.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate sources and explain, with examples from phones or the internet, why digital signals are more reliable than analog signals.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can combine scientific and technical information to support the claim that digital signals encode and send information more reliably than analog signals.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare a digital and an analog signal using pictures and say which is clearer, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name devices that send information, such as phones and radios, with picture support.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.A Structure and Function)
text: Conduct an investigation to provide evidence that living things are made of cells; either one cell or many different numbers and types of cells.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a microscope investigation to compare different cell types and explain how the evidence shows all living things are made of cells.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can conduct an investigation to provide evidence that living things are made of one cell or many different cells.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can observe cells under a microscope and label them as one cell or many cells, with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort living and non-living things and say that living things are made of cells, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.A Structure and Function)
text: Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways the parts of cells contribute to the function.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to predict what would happen to a cell if one part, such as the mitochondria or membrane, stopped working.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to describe how a cell works as a whole and how its parts help it function.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label the main parts of a cell and match each part to its job, using a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to the nucleus and cell membrane on a cell picture, with support.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.A Structure and Function)
text: Use argument supported by evidence for how the body is a system of interacting subsystems composed of groups of cells.
ee_text: Target Level: Make a claim about how a structure (e.g., organs and organ systems) and its related function supports survival of animals (circulatory, digestive, and respiratory systems). Precursor Level: Use a model to demonstrate how organs are connected in major organ systems. Initial Level: Recognize major organs of animals.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can argue with evidence how two body systems work together, such as the circulatory and respiratory systems during exercise.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use evidence to argue that the body is a system of interacting subsystems made of groups of cells.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can put cells, tissues, organs, and systems in order and give one example of each, with a graphic organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some body organs, like the heart and lungs, and say what they do, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can make a claim about how a body organ or system and its job help an animal survive.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.B Growth and Development of Organisms)
text: Use argument based on empirical evidence and scientific reasoning to support an explanation for how characteristic animal behaviors and specialized plant structures affect the probability of successful reproduction of animals and plants respectively.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence for several animal behaviors and plant structures and explain which most increases the chance of successful reproduction.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use evidence and reasoning to explain how animal behaviors and plant structures affect the chance of successful reproduction.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give an example of an animal behavior or flower part that helps reproduction and explain it with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name ways animals care for young or how flowers attract bees, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.B Growth and Development of Organisms)
text: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how environmental and genetic factors influence the growth of organisms.
ee_text: Target Level: Interpret data to show that environmental resources (e.g., food, light, space, water) influence growth of organisms (e.g., drought decreasing plant growth, fertilizer increasing plant growth, different varities of plant seeds growing at different rates in different conditions, fish growing larger in large ponds than small ponds). Precursor Level: Identify factors that influence growth of organisms. Initial Level: Match organisms to their habitats.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze data to separate genetic and environmental effects on growth and explain a real example, such as plant growth in drought.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how environmental and genetic factors affect the growth of organisms.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a data table to describe how water, light, or food changed how a plant or animal grew, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that living things need food, water, and light to grow, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use data to show that food, light, space, and water affect how living things grow.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.C Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in)
text: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for the role of photosynthesis in the cycling of matter and flow of energy into and out of organisms.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use evidence to explain how photosynthesis links matter and energy between plants, animals, and the air in an ecosystem.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for the role of photosynthesis in cycling matter and energy into and out of organisms.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can complete a diagram showing that plants use light, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugar and oxygen, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants need sunlight, water, and air to make their own food, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.C Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in)
text: Develop a model to describe how food is rearranged through chemical reactions forming new molecules that support growth and/or release energy as this matter moves through an organism.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how the same atoms from food are used both to build body parts and to release energy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to describe how food is rearranged through chemical reactions to make new molecules for growth or to release energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram to show that food is broken down in the body to give energy and help growth, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that food gives our bodies energy and helps us grow, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.D Information Processing)
text: Gather and synthesize information that sensory receptors respond to stimuli by sending messages to the brain for immediate behavior or storage as memories.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can combine information from several sources to explain how a sense receptor, nerves, and the brain work together in a fast reaction and in memory.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can gather and combine information that sensory receptors respond to stimuli and send messages to the brain for actions or memories.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how a sense organ, like the eye, sends a message to the brain, using a flow chart with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the five senses and the body part for each, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.A Interdependent Relationships in Ecosystems)
text: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence for the effects of resource availability on organisms and populations of organisms in an ecosystem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze population graphs to predict what will happen to organisms when a resource changes and explain my reasoning with data.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze and interpret data to show how resource availability affects organisms and populations in an ecosystem.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a simple graph and say how a population changed when food or water changed, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name resources that living things need, such as food, water, and space, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.A Interdependent Relationships in Ecosystems)
text: Construct an explanation that predicts patterns of interactions among organisms across multiple ecosystems.
ee_text: Target Level: Use models of food chains/webs to identify producers and consumers in aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Precursor Level: Classify animals based on what they eat (e.g., herbivore, omnivore, carnivore). Initial Level: Identify food that animals eat.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict interactions in an unfamiliar ecosystem and justify my prediction using patterns of competition, predation, and mutualism.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation that predicts patterns of interactions among organisms in different ecosystems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify predator and prey, competition, or helping relationships in an ecosystem picture, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say which animal eats which in a simple food chain, with picture support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a food chain or food web to find producers and consumers on land and in water.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.B Cycles of Matter and Energy Transfer in Ecosystems)
text: Develop a model to describe the cycling of matter and flow of energy among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain what happens to matter and energy if decomposers or producers are removed from an ecosystem.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to describe how matter cycles and energy flows among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw a food web with producers, consumers, and decomposers and show the direction of energy, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can make a simple food chain starting with the sun and a plant, using picture cards.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.C Ecosystem Dynamics, Functioning, and Resilience)
text: Construct an argument supported by empirical evidence that changes to physical or biological components of an ecosystem affect populations.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate data from a real ecosystem change, such as coral bleaching in the Gulf, and argue how it affects several populations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an argument supported by evidence that changes to physical or biological parts of an ecosystem affect populations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use data to describe how one change, like less rain, affected a population, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that living things can be harmed when their habitat changes, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.C Ecosystem Dynamics, Functioning, and Resilience)
text: Evaluate competing design solutions for maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem services.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare design solutions for protecting an ecosystem, using criteria, constraints, and data, and recommend the best one with reasons.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate competing design solutions for maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem services.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare two ways to protect a habitat and say which is better using a simple checklist, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name ways people help protect plants and animals, such as planting trees, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3 Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits (LS3.A Inheritance of Traits, LS3.B Variation of Traits)
text: Develop and use a model to describe why structural changes to genes (mutations) located on chromosomes may affect proteins and may result in harmful, beneficial, or neutral effects to the structure and function of the organism.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how one specific mutation changes a protein and predict whether its effect is harmful, helpful, or neutral.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to describe why changes to genes (mutations) may change proteins and cause harmful, helpful, or neutral effects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain with a diagram that genes are instructions and a change in a gene can change a trait, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that living things get traits from their parents, using pictures of families of animals.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3 Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits (LS3.A Inheritance of Traits, LS3.B Variation of Traits)
text: Develop and use a model to describe why asexual reproduction results in offspring with identical genetic information and sexual reproduction results in offspring with genetic variation.
ee_text: Target Level: Make a claim supported by evidence that offspring inherit traits from their parents. Precursor Level: Identify similarities and differences between plant and animal parents and their offspring (e.g., eye color, hair/fur color, height, leaf shape, and/or markings). Initial Level: Recognize that organisms differ within same species (e.g., dogs, chickens, oaks that differ in color and size).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use Punnett squares to predict offspring traits and explain why sexual reproduction gives a population more variation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to explain why asexual reproduction gives identical offspring and sexual reproduction gives offspring with variation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare pictures of asexual and sexual reproduction and say which offspring look the same as the parent, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that babies look like their parents but not exactly the same, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can make a claim with evidence that offspring get traits from their parents.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.A Evidence of Common Ancestry and Diversity)
text: Analyze and interpret data for patterns in the fossil record that document the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life forms throughout the history of life on Earth under the assumption that natural laws operate today as in the past.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze fossil data from rock layers to describe patterns of change and extinction and explain how scientists date them.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze and interpret fossil record data for patterns of existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life on Earth.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a rock layer diagram to say which fossils are older or younger, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that fossils are remains of living things from long ago, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.A Evidence of Common Ancestry and Diversity)
text: Apply scientific ideas to construct an explanation for the anatomical similarities and differences among modern organisms and between modern and fossil organisms to infer evolutionary relationships.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare anatomical structures across several modern and fossil organisms and justify which are most closely related.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation for anatomical similarities and differences among modern and fossil organisms to infer evolutionary relationships.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare bones of two animals and describe one way they are alike and one way they differ, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point out body parts that look alike in two animals, such as a human arm and a bat wing.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.A Evidence of Common Ancestry and Diversity)
text: Analyze displays of pictorial data to compare patterns of similarities in the embryological development across multiple species to identify relationships not evident in the fully formed anatomy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze embryo pictures from several species and explain how the patterns show relationships that adult forms hide.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze pictures of embryos from different species to compare patterns and identify relationships not seen in adult anatomy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare two embryo pictures and describe features that are the same, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that young animals at an early stage can look alike, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.B Natural Selection)
text: Construct an explanation based on evidence that describes how genetic variations of traits in a population increase some individuals’ probability of surviving and reproducing in a specific environment.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use data and probability to explain how a trait spreads in a population over generations in a changing environment.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation with evidence of how genetic variations in traits help some individuals survive and reproduce in a specific environment.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain why an animal with a helpful trait, like camouflage, is more likely to survive, using sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that animals of the same kind can look different, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.B Natural Selection)
text: Gather and synthesize information about technologies that have changed the way humans influence the inheritance of desired traits in organisms.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate sources about a technology such as selective breeding or genetic modification and discuss its benefits and risks.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can gather and combine information about technologies that have changed how humans influence the inheritance of desired traits.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one example of selective breeding, such as date palms or camels, using a short text with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that farmers choose the best plants and animals to grow, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.C Adaptation)
text: Use mathematical representations to support explanations of how natural selection may lead to increases and decreases of specific traits in populations over time.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a simulation and graphs to model how natural selection changes trait percentages and predict future changes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support explanations of how natural selection increases or decreases traits in populations over time.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a bar graph to describe how the number of animals with a trait changed over time, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can count animals with and without a trait in a picture and record it in a table, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.A The Universe and its Stars, ESS1.B Earth and the Solar System)
text: Develop and use a model of the Earth-sun-moon system to describe the cyclic patterns of lunar phases, eclipses of the sun and moon, and seasons.
ee_text: Target Level: Use an Earth-Sun-Moon model to show that Earth's orbit around the Sun corresponds to a calendar year and the orbit of the Moon around Earth corresponds to a month. Precursor Level: Use a model to show that Earth's Moon moves around Earth, and Earth and its Moon move around the Sun. Initial Level: Recognize models of the Earth, Moon, and Sun system.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to predict moon phases and eclipses and explain why seasons in Qatar differ from seasons in the southern hemisphere.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model of the Earth-sun-moon system to describe patterns of lunar phases, eclipses, and seasons.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a physical model to show how the moon orbits Earth and name the main moon phases, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth spins and moves around the sun and the moon moves around Earth, using a model.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use an Earth-sun-moon model to show that one Earth orbit is a year and one moon orbit is about a month.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.A The Universe and its Stars, ESS1.B Earth and the Solar System)
text: Develop and use a model to describe the role of gravity in the motions within galaxies and the solar system.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how gravity keeps planets in orbit and predict what would happen if the sun's gravity were weaker.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to describe the role of gravity in the motions within galaxies and the solar system.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram to explain that gravity keeps planets moving around the sun, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the sun and planets and say that planets move around the sun, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.B Earth and the Solar System)
text: Analyze and interpret data to determine scale properties of objects in the solar system.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze data to compare planets and moons and build a scale model that shows sizes and distances.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze and interpret data to determine scale properties of objects in the solar system.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a data table to compare the size or distance of two planets, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort solar system objects from smallest to largest using pictures, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.C The History of Planet Earth)
text: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence from rock strata for how the geologic time scale is used to organize Earth’s 4.6-billion-year-old history.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use rock layer and fossil evidence to place major events on the geologic time scale and explain how scientists know their order.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence from rock layers for how the geologic time scale organizes Earth's 4.6-billion-year history.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can put events from Earth's history in order on a timeline using rock layer clues, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that lower rock layers are usually older than upper layers, using a diagram.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.A Earth Materials and Systems)
text: Develop a model to describe the cycling of Earth’s materials and the flow of energy that drives this process.
ee_text: Target Level: Use a model to describe the change within the rock cycle between igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rock. Precursor Level: Use a model to describe the change from igneous to sedimentary rock. Initial Level: Identify the process that forms igneous rock (e.g., volcanoes).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how energy from the sun and Earth's interior drives the rock cycle and predict how a rock will change.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to describe how Earth's materials cycle and the energy flow that drives this process.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can complete a rock cycle diagram and name the processes, such as melting and weathering, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the three types of rock, using pictures and samples.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a model to show how igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks change into each other.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.A Earth Materials and Systems, ESS2.C The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface)
text: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how geoscience processes have changed Earth’s surface at varying time and spatial scales.
ee_text: Target Level: Explain how geoscience processes that occur daily (e.g.,wind, rain, runoff) slowly change the surface of Earth, while catastrophic events (e.g., earthquakes, tornadoes, floods) can quickly change the surface of Earth. Precursor Level: Identify geoscience processes (e.g., wind, rain, runoff) that have an impact on landforms (e.g., landslides, erosion such as gullies). Initial Level: Identify differences in weather conditions from day to day.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare fast and slow geoscience processes with evidence and explain how both shaped a real landform, such as wadis or sand dunes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how geoscience processes have changed Earth's surface at different time and space scales.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how wind, water, or earthquakes change land, using pictures and sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that wind and water can move sand and rock, using a demonstration.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can explain how wind and rain change Earth's surface slowly and how events like floods and earthquakes change it quickly.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.B Plate Tectonics and Large-Scale System)
text: Analyze and interpret data on the distribution of fossils and rocks, continental shapes, and seafloor structures to provide evidence of the past plate motions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can combine fossil, rock, and seafloor data to argue how continents moved and predict future plate motions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze and interpret data on fossils, rocks, continent shapes, and seafloor structures to show evidence of past plate motions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can fit continent shapes together like a puzzle and describe matching fossils, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth's continents are on large moving pieces, using a map.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.C The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface)
text: Develop a model to describe the cycling of water through Earth’s systems driven by energy from the sun and the force of gravity.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model of the water cycle to explain how the sun and gravity drive each step and apply it to water in Qatar.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to describe how water cycles through Earth's systems, driven by energy from the sun and the force of gravity.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label evaporation, condensation, and precipitation on a water cycle diagram, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that water can be liquid, solid, or gas and that rain comes from clouds, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.C The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface, ESS2.D Weather and Climate)
text: Collect data to provide evidence for how the motions and complex interactions of air masses result in changes in weather conditions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can collect and analyze weather data to explain how moving air masses caused a weather change and predict the next day's weather.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can collect data to provide evidence for how motions and interactions of air masses cause changes in weather.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can record temperature and wind data for several days and describe a change, with a data table.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe today's weather using words like hot, windy, or humid, with picture support.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.C The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface, ESS2.D Weather and Climate)
text: Develop and use a model to describe how unequal heating and rotation of the Earth cause patterns of atmospheric and oceanic circulation that determine regional climates.
ee_text: Target Level: Interpret basic weather information (e.g., radar, map) to make predictions about future conditions (e.g., precipitation, temperature, wind). Precursor Level: Interpret basic weather information (e.g., radar, map) to compare weather conditions (either over several days at the same location or different locations on the same day). Initial Level: Interpret basic weather information (e.g., radar, map) to identify weather conditions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how unequal heating, Earth's rotation, and ocean currents together create the climate of a region such as the Gulf.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to describe how unequal heating and Earth's rotation cause atmospheric and ocean circulation that shapes regional climates.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram to show that the equator gets more heat than the poles and that this moves air, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that some places on Earth are hot and some are cold, using a globe or map.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can read weather maps or radar to predict rain, temperature, or wind.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.A Natural Resources)
text: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how the uneven distributions of Earth’s mineral, energy, and groundwater resources are the result of past and current geoscience processes.
ee_text: Target Level: Interpret, based on evidence, how the geoscience processes (e.g., weathering, erosion) create resources. Precursor Level: Identify the geoscience process that produces a natural resource (e.g., solar energy creating wind energy, rock cycle with ores and minerals). Initial Level: Identify a natural resource (e.g., water, sand, wind).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence why oil, gas, and groundwater are found in some places, such as Qatar, and not others, and how use changes their supply.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how uneven distributions of minerals, energy, and groundwater result from past and current geoscience processes.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a map to show where a resource like oil or water is found and say one reason why, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name natural resources, such as water, oil, and gas, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use evidence to explain how weathering and erosion make natural resources.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.B Natural Hazards)
text: Analyze and interpret data on natural hazards to forecast future catastrophic events and inform the development of technologies to mitigate their effects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze hazard data to forecast a future event and evaluate which technology would best reduce its effects.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze and interpret data on natural hazards to forecast future events and inform technologies that reduce their effects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a hazard map or graph and describe where or when a hazard is likely, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name natural hazards, such as sandstorms, floods, and earthquakes, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.C Human Impacts on Earth Systems)
text: Apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and minimizing a human impact on the environment.
ee_text: Target Level: Develop a plan to monitor and minimize a human impact on the local environment (e.g., water, land, pollution). Precursor Level: Recognize ways in which humans impact the environment (e.g., agriculture, pollution, recycling, city growth). Initial Level: Recognize resources (e.g., food, water, shelter, air) in the local environment that are important for human life.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design, test, and improve a method to monitor and reduce a local human impact, such as plastic waste on beaches, using data.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and minimizing a human impact on the environment.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can choose a human impact and suggest one way to measure it and one way to reduce it, with a planning template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name ways people harm the environment, such as littering, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can make a plan to check and reduce a human impact on my local environment.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.C Human Impacts on Earth Systems)
text: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how increases in human population and per-capita consumption of natural resources impact Earth’s systems.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use data to argue how population growth and resource use affect several Earth systems and propose ways to reduce the impact.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an argument supported by evidence for how growing human population and resource use per person impact Earth's systems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a graph to describe how more people use more water or energy, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people use water, food, and energy every day, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.D Global Climate Change)
text: Ask questions to clarify evidence of the factors that have caused the rise in global temperatures over the past century.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask and refine questions to evaluate evidence for human and natural causes of rising temperatures and identify which evidence is strongest.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask questions to clarify evidence of the factors that have caused the rise in global temperatures over the past century.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask a question about a temperature graph and name one cause of warming, with question stems.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can read a thermometer and say whether it is getting hotter, using a simple graph with help.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.A Defining Engineering Problems)
text: Define the criteria and constraints of a design problem with sufficient precision to ensure a successful solution, taking into account relevant scientific principles and potential impacts on people and the natural environment that may limit possible solutions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can define a design problem with precise, measurable criteria and constraints and explain how science ideas and impacts on people and nature shape them.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can define the criteria and constraints of a design problem precisely, considering science principles and impacts on people and the environment.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can list what a design must do (criteria) and its limits (constraints), using a template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe a problem that a new tool or object could solve, with teacher support.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions)
text: Evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process to determine how well they meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build a weighted decision matrix to compare designs and justify which best meets the criteria and constraints.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process to see how well they meet the criteria and constraints.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a checklist to compare two designs against the criteria, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say which of two designs I like better and give one reason, using sentence frames.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions)

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions, ETS1.C Optimizing the Design Solution)
text: Analyze data from tests to determine similarities and differences among several design solutions to identify the best characteristics of each that can be combined into a new solution to better meet the criteria for success.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze test data from several designs and combine their best features into a new design that performs better.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze test data to find similarities and differences among designs and combine the best features into a new solution.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read test results for two designs and say which part of each worked best, with a data table.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can test a design and say whether it worked, with teacher guidance.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions, ETS1.C Optimizing the Design Solution)
text: Develop a model to generate data for iterative testing and modification of a proposed object, tool, or process such that an optimal design can be achieved.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to generate data, run several rounds of testing, and justify how each change moved my design closer to optimal.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to generate data for testing and improving a proposed object, tool, or process until an optimal design is reached.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can build and test a model, record results, and make one improvement, with step-by-step support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can build a simple model of my idea using provided materials, with help.

cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions, ETS1.C Optimizing the Design Solution)
