subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter)
text: Use the periodic table as a model to predict the relative properties of elements based on the patterns of electrons in the outermost energy level of atoms.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use valence electron patterns to predict and explain the properties of an unfamiliar element and how it will bond.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the periodic table to predict relative properties of elements from the patterns of electrons in their outer energy level.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find an element's group and period and say how many valence electrons it has, with a periodic table guide.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find elements on the periodic table and identify metals and nonmetals, with support.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter, PS1.B Chemical Reactions)
text: Construct and revise an explanation for the outcome of a simple chemical reaction based on the outermost electron states of atoms, trends in the periodic table, and knowledge of the patterns of chemical properties.
ee_text: Target Level: Make a claim supported by evidence to explain patterns of chemical properties that occur in a substance during a common chemical reaction (e.g., baking soda and vinegar). Precursor Level: Identify the changes that have occurred during a chemical reaction (e.g., metal-rust, paper-burn). Initial Level: Recognize that a change has occurred during a chemical reaction.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict products of reactions I have not seen before and revise my explanation when new data disagrees with it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct and revise an explanation for the outcome of a simple chemical reaction using outer electron states and periodic table trends.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain why sodium and chlorine form a compound using valence electrons, with a worked example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify reactants and products in a simple chemical equation, with labels.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can make a claim with evidence about the changes I see in a common reaction, such as baking soda and vinegar.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter)
text: Plan and conduct an investigation to gather evidence to compare the structure of substances at the bulk scale to infer the strength of electrical forces between particles.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design an investigation of melting points or solubility and use the results to rank attractive forces between particles in several substances.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct an investigation comparing bulk properties of substances to infer the strength of electrical forces between particles.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can follow a procedure to compare melting or boiling points and say which substance has stronger forces, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe physical properties such as melting point and hardness, using a word bank.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter, PS1.B Chemical Reactions)
text: Develop a model to illustrate that the release or absorption of energy from a chemical reaction system depends upon the changes in total bond energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use bond energy values to calculate whether a reaction is exothermic or endothermic and explain the result with an energy diagram.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to show that the energy released or absorbed in a reaction depends on changes in total bond energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read an energy diagram and say if a reaction releases or absorbs energy, with guided questions.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that some reactions get hot and some get cold, using lab observations.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.B Chemical Reactions)
text: Apply scientific principles and evidence to provide an explanation about the effects of changing the temperature or concentration of the reacting particles on the rate at which a reaction occurs.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use collision theory and data to predict how changing temperature and concentration together will affect a reaction rate.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can apply scientific principles and evidence to explain how changing temperature or concentration affects the rate of a reaction.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe from lab data that warmer or more concentrated solutions react faster, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can time a simple reaction and say whether it was fast or slow, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.B Chemical Reactions)
text: Refine the design of a chemical system by specifying a change in conditions that would produce increased amounts of products at equilibrium.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply Le Chatelier's principle to an industrial process, such as ammonia production, and justify the best conditions for product yield.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can refine the design of a chemical system by choosing a change in conditions that increases the amount of product at equilibrium.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can predict which way an equilibrium shifts when one condition changes, using a guide.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe that some reactions go both forward and backward, with a diagram.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.B Chemical Reactions)
text: Use mathematical representations to support the claim that atoms, and therefore mass, are conserved during a chemical reaction.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use mole ratios and mass data to show conservation of mass and calculate the mass of product from a given reactant.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support the claim that atoms, and so mass, are conserved during a chemical reaction.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can balance a simple chemical equation and count atoms on each side, with step-by-step support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can count the atoms of each element in a chemical formula, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.C Nuclear Processes)
text: Develop models to illustrate the changes in the composition of the nucleus of the atom and the energy released during the processes of fission, fusion, and radioactive decay.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare fission, fusion, and radioactive decay using nuclear equations and explain their uses and risks for energy production.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop models to show how the nucleus changes and energy is released during fission, fusion, and radioactive decay.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use diagrams to describe the difference between fission and fusion, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name protons and neutrons as particles in the nucleus, using a model.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.A Forces and Motion)
text: Analyze data to support the claim that Newton’s second law of motion describes the mathematical relationship among the net force on a macroscopic object, its mass, and its acceleration.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze motion data from a new situation, calculate net force, and predict acceleration using F = ma.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze data to support the claim that Newton's second law describes the relationship among net force, mass, and acceleration.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use F = ma to solve a simple problem and read a velocity-time graph, with a worked example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that a bigger force makes an object speed up more, using a demonstration.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.A Forces and Motion)
text: Use mathematical representations to support the claim that the total momentum of a system of objects is conserved when there is no net force on the system.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use momentum calculations to analyze a real collision, such as a car crash, and explain what the results show.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support the claim that total momentum of a system is conserved when there is no net force.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can calculate momentum (p = mv) for objects before and after a collision, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that heavier or faster objects are harder to stop, using examples.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.A Forces and Motion)
text: Apply scientific and engineering ideas to design, evaluate, and refine a device that minimizes the force on a macroscopic object during a collision.
ee_text: Target Level: Evaluate the effectiveness of safety devices and design a solution that could minimize the force of a collision. Precursor Level: Use data to compare the effectiveness of safety devices to determine which best minimizes the force of a collision. Initial Level: Identify safety equipment devices that minimize force of a collision (e.g., floor mats, helmets, or steel-toed boots).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can test and refine my collision device using data and explain how it reduces force by increasing collision time.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can apply science and engineering ideas to design, evaluate, and refine a device that minimizes force on an object during a collision.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can build a device such as an egg-drop container and describe how it protects the object, with a design template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name safety devices that protect people in crashes, such as seatbelts and helmets, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can judge how well safety devices work and design a solution that lowers the force of a collision.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.B Types of Interactions)
text: Use mathematical representations of Newton’s Law of Gravitation and Coulomb’s Law to describe and predict the gravitational and electrostatic forces between objects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use both laws to compare gravitational and electric forces and predict how changing distance or mass or charge changes the force.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use Newton's Law of Gravitation and Coulomb's Law to describe and predict gravitational and electrostatic forces between objects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a formula with given values to calculate a gravitational or electric force, with a worked example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that masses attract each other and that charges can attract or repel, using diagrams.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.B Types of Interactions)
text: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that an electric current can produce a magnetic field and that a changing magnetic field can produce an electric current.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design an investigation that shows both effects and apply them to explain how a generator or motor works.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct an investigation to show that an electric current makes a magnetic field and a changing magnetic field makes a current.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can follow a lab procedure with a coil and compass to observe a magnetic effect from current, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can build a simple circuit and say when current is flowing, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.B Types of Interactions)
text: Communicate scientific and technical information about why the molecular-level structure is important in the functioning of designed materials.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how the molecular structure of a designed material, such as a polymer, gives it a property and suggest a design improvement.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can communicate scientific and technical information about why molecular-level structure is important to how designed materials work.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one material's structure makes it strong or flexible, using a text and diagram with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name everyday designed materials and one property of each, such as plastic is flexible.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.A Definitions of Energy, PS3.B Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer)
text: Create a computational model to calculate the change in the energy of one component in a system when the change in energy of the other component(s) and energy flows in and out of the system are known.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build a computational model, such as a spreadsheet, that tracks energy in a system and test it against real data.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create a computational model to calculate the energy change of one part of a system when other energy changes and flows are known.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use energy equations to calculate a missing energy value in a simple system, with a worked example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name forms of energy, such as kinetic, potential, and thermal, using examples.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.A Definitions of Energy)
text: Develop and use models to illustrate that energy at the macroscopic scale can be accounted for as a combination of energy associated with the motion of particles (objects) and energy associated with the relative position of particles (objects).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain energy changes at both the particle and object level in a real system, such as a pendulum or heated gas.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use models to show that energy can be explained as motion energy plus energy of relative position of particles or objects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label kinetic and potential energy at points on a roller coaster diagram, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that moving objects have energy and raised objects have stored energy, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.A Definitions of Energy)
text: Design, build, and refine a device that works within given constraints to convert one form of energy into another form of energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design, test, and refine an energy-converting device, calculate its efficiency, and justify design changes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can design, build, and refine a device that works within constraints to convert one form of energy into another.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can build a device from a plan, such as a solar oven or simple motor, and describe the energy change, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a device that changes energy from one form to another, such as a lamp.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.B Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer)
text: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that the transfer of thermal energy when two components of different temperature are combined within a closed system results in a more uniform energy distribution among the components in the system (second law of thermodynamics).
ee_text: Target Level: Investigate and predict the temperatures of two liquids before and after combining to show uniform energy distribution. Precursor Level: Compare the temperatures of two liquids of different temperatures before and after combining. Initial Level: Compare relative difference in temperature (warmth, coldness) of two liquids.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use calorimetry data to calculate heat transfer and explain how the results show the second law of thermodynamics.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct an investigation to show that mixing objects at different temperatures in a closed system leads to a more even energy distribution.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can mix hot and cold water, record temperatures, and describe that they reach the same temperature, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that heat moves from hot objects to cold objects, using a demonstration.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can predict and measure the temperatures of two liquids before and after mixing to show the energy spreads out evenly.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.C Relationship Between Energy and Forces)
text: Develop and use a model of two objects interacting through electric or magnetic fields to illustrate the forces between objects and the changes in energy of the objects due to the interaction.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a field model to predict how forces and energy change as two charged or magnetic objects move closer or farther apart.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model of two objects interacting through electric or magnetic fields to show the forces and energy changes.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw field lines between two magnets or charges and describe the force, with a diagram guide.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can observe that magnets push or pull each other without touching, with support.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.A Wave Properties)
text: Use mathematical representations to support a claim regarding relationships among the frequency, wavelength, and speed of waves traveling in various media.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use the wave equation to solve problems in different media and explain why wave speed changes from air to water.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support a claim about how frequency, wavelength, and speed of waves are related in different media.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use v = f x wavelength to calculate one missing value, with a worked example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can label wavelength and amplitude on a wave diagram, with a word bank.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.A Wave Properties)
text: Evaluate questions about the advantages of using digital transmission and storage of information.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the advantages and drawbacks of digital storage and transmission, including security and data loss, using evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate questions about the advantages of digital transmission and storage of information.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can list advantages of digital information, such as copying without loss, using a text with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name devices that store digital information, such as phones and USB drives.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.A Wave Properties, PS4.B Electromagnetic Radiation)
text: Evaluate the claims, evidence, and reasoning behind the idea that electromagnetic radiation can be described either by a wave model or a particle model, and that for some situations one model is more useful than the other.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence from experiments such as the photoelectric effect and explain when the particle model or wave model is more useful.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate claims, evidence, and reasoning that light can be described by a wave model or a particle model, each useful in some situations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one piece of evidence for the wave model and one for the particle model of light, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that light travels and can be reflected, using a demonstration.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.B Electromagnetic Radiation)
text: Evaluate the validity and reliability of claims in published materials of the effects that different frequencies of electromagnetic radiation have when absorbed by matter.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can critique published claims about radiation, such as phone signals or UV light, and judge their reliability using scientific evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate the validity and reliability of published claims about effects of different frequencies of electromagnetic radiation absorbed by matter.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare the energy of radio waves, UV, and X-rays and name one effect of each, using a chart.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name types of electromagnetic radiation, such as light and X-rays, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.A Wave Properties, PS4.B Electromagnetic Radiation, PS4.C Information Technologies and)
text: Communicate technical information about how some technological devices use the principles of wave behavior and wave interactions with matter to transmit and capture information and energy.
ee_text: Target Level: Make a claim supported by evidence that shows how some devices use light and sound waves to transmit and capture information. Precursor Level: Identify common devices which use light or sound waves to transmit information. Initial Level: Identify how common technological devices are used for different purposes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain in detail how a device such as a solar panel or fiber optic cable uses wave behavior, and suggest an improvement.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can communicate technical information about how devices use wave behavior and wave interactions with matter to send and capture information and energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one device, such as a phone or microwave, uses waves, using a diagram and sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name devices that use waves, such as radios and phones, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can make a claim with evidence about how devices use light and sound waves to send and receive information.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.A Structure and Function)
text: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the structure of DNA determines the structure of proteins, which carry out the essential functions of life through systems of specialized cells.
ee_text: Target Level: Explain how different organs of the body carry out essential functions of life. Precursor Level: Indicate the function of major organs of the body. Initial Level: Identify major organs of the body.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a change in a DNA sequence changes a protein and affects a body function, using a real example such as sickle cell.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how DNA structure determines protein structure, which carries out life functions in specialized cells.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe that DNA carries instructions to make proteins, using a diagram and word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that DNA is found in the nucleus of cells, using a picture.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can explain how different body organs do the jobs that keep us alive.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.A Structure and Function)
text: Develop and use a model to illustrate the hierarchical organization of interacting systems that provide specific functions within multicellular organisms.
ee_text: Target Level: Use a model to illustrate the organization and interaction of major organs into systems (e.g., circulatory, respiratory, digestive, sensory) in the body to provide specific functions. Precursor Level: Identify which organs work for a specific function. Initial Level: Recognize that different organs have different functions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how several body systems interact to respond to a challenge, such as exercise or illness.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to show the hierarchy of interacting systems that perform specific functions in multicellular organisms.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can order cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems and give an example of each, with a graphic organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name major organs and say what they do, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a model to show how organs work together in body systems to do specific jobs.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.A Structure and Function)
text: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that feedback mechanisms maintain homeostasis.
ee_text: Target Level: Collect data from an investigation to show how different organisms react to changes (e.g., heart rate increases with exercise, pupils react to light). Precursor Level: Compare before and after data on changes that occur to an organism. Initial Level: Identify changes in the data display (e.g. objects, pictures, graphs, charts, etc.).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design an investigation of a feedback mechanism, analyze the data, and explain how the body returns to balance.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct an investigation to show that feedback mechanisms maintain homeostasis.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can measure heart rate before and after exercise and describe how the body returns to normal, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that the body sweats to cool down and shivers to warm up, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can collect data to show how living things react to changes, such as heart rate rising with exercise.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.B Growth and Development of Organisms)
text: Use a model to illustrate the role of cellular division (mitosis) and differentiation in producing and maintaining complex organisms.
ee_text: Target Level: Use a model to illustrate how growth occurs when cells multiply. Precursor Level: Use a model to relate the number of cells to the size of a body. Initial Level: Recognize that organisms are composed of cells.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how mitosis and differentiation build and repair tissues and what happens when division is uncontrolled.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use a model to show the role of mitosis and differentiation in producing and maintaining complex organisms.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can put the stages of mitosis in order using diagrams and a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that cells divide to make new cells for growth and repair, using a picture.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a model to show that living things grow when cells multiply.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.C Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in)
text: Use a model to illustrate how photosynthesis transforms light energy into stored chemical energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to trace energy and matter through photosynthesis and explain how limiting factors affect its rate.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use a model to show how photosynthesis changes light energy into stored chemical energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label the inputs and outputs of photosynthesis on a diagram, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants use sunlight to make food, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.C Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in)
text: Construct and revise an explanation based on evidence for how carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen from sugar molecules may combine with other elements to form amino acids and/or other large carbon-based molecules.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can trace atoms from sugar into proteins, fats, and other molecules and revise my explanation using new evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct and revise an explanation for how carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen from sugars combine with other elements to form large carbon-based molecules.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify carbohydrates, proteins, and fats and the elements they contain, using a chart.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name foods that contain sugar, protein, or fat, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.C Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in)
text: Use a model to illustrate that cellular respiration is a chemical process whereby the bonds of food molecules and oxygen molecules are broken and the bonds in new compounds are formed, resulting in a net transfer of energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare photosynthesis and cellular respiration as linked processes and explain the energy transfer in terms of bonds broken and formed.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use a model to show that cellular respiration breaks bonds in food and oxygen and forms new compounds, transferring energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label the inputs and outputs of cellular respiration on a diagram, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that our cells use food and oxygen to get energy, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.A Interdependent Relationships in Ecosystems)
text: Use mathematical and/or computational representations to support explanations of factors that affect carrying capacity of ecosystems at different scales.
ee_text: Target Level: Use a graphical representation to explain changes over time in the population size of an animal species (e.g., currently on the endangered list). Precursor Level: Use a graphical representation to show changes in population size. Initial Level: Recognize that there was a change in the population size.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use population data and a model to predict carrying capacity and explain how changing one factor shifts it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical or computational representations to support explanations of factors that affect carrying capacity of ecosystems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a population graph and identify where it levels off at carrying capacity, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that an area can only support a limited number of animals, using examples.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a graph to explain how the population of an animal, such as an endangered species, changed over time.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.A Interdependent Relationships in Ecosystems, LS2.C Ecosystem Dynamics, Functioning, and Resilience)
text: Use mathematical representations to support and revise explanations based on evidence about factors affecting biodiversity and populations in ecosystems of different scales.
ee_text: Target Level: Use a graphical representation to explain the dependence of an animal population on other organisms for food and their environment for shelter. Precursor Level: Recognize the relationship between population size and available resources for food and shelter from a graphical representation. Initial Level: Identify food and shelter needs for familiar wildlife.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze biodiversity data from different ecosystems, calculate changes, and revise my explanation based on new evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support and revise explanations about factors affecting biodiversity and populations in ecosystems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can calculate a simple population change from data and name one factor that caused it, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can count species in a sample area and record them in a table, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a graph to explain how an animal population depends on other living things for food and on its environment for shelter.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.B Cycles of Matter and Energy Transfer in Ecosystems)
text: Construct and revise an explanation based on evidence for the cycling of matter and flow of energy in aerobic and anaerobic conditions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare energy yield in aerobic and anaerobic conditions and explain real examples, such as muscle fatigue or bread making.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct and revise an explanation based on evidence for cycling of matter and flow of energy in aerobic and anaerobic conditions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration using a chart, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that most living things need oxygen to get energy from food.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.B Cycles of Matter and Energy Transfer in Ecosystems)
text: Use mathematical representations to support claims for the cycling of matter and flow of energy among organisms in an ecosystem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can calculate energy transfer across trophic levels using the 10 percent rule and explain why food chains are short.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support claims about cycling of matter and flow of energy among organisms in an ecosystem.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use an energy pyramid to show that energy decreases at each level, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can build a food chain and name producers and consumers, using picture cards.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.B Cycles of Matter and Energy Transfer in Ecosystems)
text: Develop a model to illustrate the role of photosynthesis and cellular respiration in the cycling of carbon among the biosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, and geosphere.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a carbon cycle model to explain how burning fossil fuels and deforestation change carbon in each sphere.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to show the role of photosynthesis and cellular respiration in cycling carbon among the biosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, and geosphere.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can complete a carbon cycle diagram showing where photosynthesis and respiration move carbon, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants take in carbon dioxide and animals breathe it out, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.C Ecosystem Dynamics, Functioning, and Resilience)
text: Evaluate claims, evidence, and reasoning that the complex interactions in ecosystems maintain relatively consistent numbers and types of organisms in stable conditions, but changing conditions may result in a new ecosystem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence from a real ecosystem disturbance and argue whether it will recover or become a new ecosystem.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate claims, evidence, and reasoning that ecosystems stay stable in stable conditions but changing conditions can create a new ecosystem.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a case study to describe how an ecosystem changed after a disturbance, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name events that change ecosystems, such as floods and fires, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS4.D Biodiversity and Humans)
text: Design, evaluate, and refine a solution for reducing the impacts of human activities on the environment and biodiversity.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design, test, and refine a solution to a local biodiversity problem, such as protecting mangroves in Qatar, using data and trade-offs.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can design, evaluate, and refine a solution for reducing the impacts of human activities on the environment and biodiversity.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can propose a solution to a human impact on biodiversity and list its pros and cons, with a template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name human activities that harm the environment, such as pollution, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.D Social Interactions and Group Behavior)
text: Evaluate evidence for the role of group behavior on individual and species’ chances to survive and reproduce.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence from studies of several species and explain how group behavior increases survival and reproduction.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate evidence for the role of group behavior in individuals' and species' chances to survive and reproduce.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one example of group behavior, such as fish schooling, and how it helps survival, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name animals that live in groups, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3 Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits (LS1.A Structure and Function, LS3.A Inheritance of Traits)
text: Ask questions to clarify relationships about the role of DNA and chromosomes in coding the instructions for characteristic traits passed from parents to offspring.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask and refine questions that connect genes, chromosomes, and proteins to explain how a specific trait is inherited.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask questions to clarify how DNA and chromosomes code instructions for traits passed from parents to offspring.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask a question about how traits are passed on and use a diagram of chromosomes to answer it, with question stems.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that children get traits from both parents, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3 Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits (LS3.B Variation of Traits)
text: Make and defend a claim based on evidence that inheritable genetic variations may result from (1) new genetic combinations through meiosis, (2) viable errors occurring during replication, and/or (3) mutations caused by environmental factors.
ee_text: Target Level: Defend why reproduction may or may not result in offspring with different traits. Precursor Level: Make a claim supported by evidence that parents and offspring may have different traits. Initial Level: Compare traits of parents and offspring.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can defend a claim about which source of variation best explains a specific case, using evidence from meiosis, replication errors, or mutations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can make and defend a claim with evidence that inheritable variation comes from meiosis, replication errors, or environmental mutations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one way new genetic variation happens, such as crossing over in meiosis, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that siblings look different from each other, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can explain why offspring may or may not have different traits from their parents.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3 Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits (LS3.B Variation of Traits)
text: Apply concepts of statistics and probability to explain the variation and distribution of expressed traits in a population.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use probability and population data to predict trait frequencies and explain differences between predicted and observed results.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can apply statistics and probability to explain the variation and distribution of expressed traits in a population.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a Punnett square to predict the chance of a trait, with a worked example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can collect data on a trait, such as height, in my class and display it in a chart, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.A Evidence of Common Ancestry and Diversity)
text: Communicate scientific information that common ancestry and biological evolution are supported by multiple lines of empirical evidence.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can combine several lines of evidence, such as DNA, fossils, and anatomy, to argue for common ancestry of a group of organisms.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can communicate scientific information that common ancestry and evolution are supported by multiple lines of evidence.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one line of evidence for evolution, such as fossils or similar bones, using sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that fossils show living things from long ago, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.B Natural Selection, LS4.C Adaptation)
text: Construct an explanation based on evidence that the process of evolution primarily results from four factors: (1) the potential for a species to increase in number, (2) the heritable genetic variation of individuals in a species due to mutation and sexual reproduction, (3) competition for limited resources, and (4) the proliferation of those organisms that are better able to survive and reproduce in the environment.
ee_text: Target Level: Explain how the traits of particular species that allow them to survive in their specific environments. Precursor Level: Identify factors in an environment that require special traits to survive. Initial Level: Match particular species to their various environments.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use the four factors to explain evolution in a new example and predict how changing one factor would change the outcome.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain with evidence that evolution results from population growth potential, genetic variation, competition for resources, and better survival and reproduction.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name the four factors of evolution and match each to an example, with a graphic organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that animals compete for food and that some survive better than others.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can explain how the traits of a species help it survive in its environment.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.B Natural Selection, LS4.C Adaptation)
text: Apply concepts of statistics and probability to support explanations that organisms with an advantageous heritable trait tend to increase in proportion to organisms lacking this trait.
ee_text: Target Level: Interpret data sets to identify an advantageous heritable trait. Precursor Level: Using data sets, identify organisms that would survive better in certain environment. Initial Level: Recognize that some organisms survive better in certain environments.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze data over generations to calculate changes in trait frequency and explain them using probability.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can apply statistics and probability to support explanations that organisms with helpful inherited traits increase in proportion over time.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a graph showing a trait increasing over generations and explain why, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can count organisms with a trait in a simulation and record it, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use data to find a helpful trait that is passed from parents to offspring.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.C Adaptation)
text: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how natural selection leads to adaptation of populations.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how natural selection produced an adaptation in a real population, such as antibiotic resistance.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how natural selection leads to adaptation of populations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe an adaptation and how it helps an organism survive in its environment, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name an adaptation, such as a camel's hump, and say what it helps with.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.C Adaptation)
text: Evaluate the evidence supporting claims that changes in environmental conditions may result in (1) increases in the number of individuals of some species, (2) the emergence of new species over time, and (3) the extinction of other species.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence from a real case to argue whether environmental change led to population growth, new species, or extinction.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate evidence that environmental changes may increase some species, produce new species, and cause others to go extinct.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one environmental change affected a species, using a case study and support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that some animals have gone extinct, using pictures and examples.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.C Adaptation, LS4.D Biodiversity and Humans)
text: Create or revise a simulation to test a solution to mitigate adverse impacts of human activity on biodiversity.
ee_text: Target Level: Evaluate a strategy to protect a species. Precursor Level: Using a mathematical model, determine which human actions help or harm a species. Initial Level: Identify a human activity that has an effect on a species.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create and revise a simulation, test several solutions, and recommend the best way to protect a species using results.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create or revise a simulation to test a solution that reduces harmful human impacts on biodiversity.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can run a given simulation, change one variable, and describe how it affected biodiversity, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name an endangered animal, such as the Arabian oryx, and one threat to it.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can judge how well a plan protects a species.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.A The Universe and its Stars)
text: Develop a model based on evidence to illustrate the life span of the sun and the role of nuclear fusion in the sun’s core to release energy that eventually reaches Earth in the form of radiation.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use evidence to model the sun's life cycle and explain how fusion energy travels to Earth and affects life.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model based on evidence of the sun's life span and how nuclear fusion in its core releases energy that reaches Earth as radiation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram to describe that the sun makes energy by fusion and sends it to Earth as light, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun is a star that gives Earth light and heat.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.A The Universe and its Stars)
text: Construct an explanation of the Big Bang theory based on astronomical evidence of light spectra, motion of distant galaxies, and composition of matter in the universe.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate several pieces of evidence, such as redshift and cosmic background radiation, and explain how each supports the Big Bang theory.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation of the Big Bang theory based on evidence from light spectra, galaxy motion, and composition of matter.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one piece of evidence for the Big Bang, such as galaxies moving apart, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that the universe is very old and very large, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.A The Universe and its Stars)
text: Communicate scientific ideas about the way stars, over their life cycle, produce elements.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how stars of different masses produce different elements and connect this to elements found on Earth.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can communicate scientific ideas about how stars produce elements during their life cycle.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the main stages in a star's life cycle using a diagram and word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that stars are born, change, and die, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.B Earth and the Solar System)
text: Use mathematical or computational representations to predict the motion of orbiting objects in the solar system.
ee_text: Target Level: Use a model of Earth and the Sun to show how Earth's tilt and orbit around the Sun cause changes in seasons. Precursor Level: Use a model of Earth and sun to show how Earth’s positions in its orbit around the Sun correspond with the four seasons. Initial Level: Identify characteristics of the seasons.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use Kepler's laws and data to predict the orbit of a planet or satellite and explain the results.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical or computational representations to predict the motion of orbiting objects in the solar system.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a given formula or simulation to compare orbital periods of two planets, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that planets move around the sun in paths called orbits, using a model.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a model of Earth and the sun to show how Earth's tilt and orbit cause the seasons.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.C The History of Planet Earth)
text: Evaluate evidence of the past and current movements of continental and oceanic crust and the theory of plate tectonics to explain the ages of crustal rocks.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze rock age data across a mid-ocean ridge and use plate tectonics to explain the pattern and predict ages at new locations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate evidence of crust movement and the theory of plate tectonics to explain the ages of crustal rocks.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a map to describe that rocks get older moving away from a mid-ocean ridge, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth's crust is broken into plates that move, using a map.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.C The History of Planet Earth)
text: Apply scientific reasoning and evidence from ancient Earth materials, meteorites, and other planetary surfaces to construct an account of Earth’s formation and early history.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can combine evidence from meteorites, moon rocks, and ancient Earth minerals to build a detailed account of Earth's early history.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can apply reasoning and evidence from ancient Earth materials, meteorites, and other planets to construct an account of Earth's formation and early history.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one type of evidence scientists use to learn how old Earth is, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth is billions of years old, using a timeline with help.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.A Earth Materials and Systems)
text: Develop a model to illustrate how Earth’s internal and surface processes operate at different spatial and temporal scales to form continental and ocean-floor features.
ee_text: Target Level: Use a model to show how constructive forces (e.g., volcanoes) and destructive mechanisms (e.g., weathering, coastal erosions) change Earth's surface. Precursor Level: Recognize if processes that change Earth's surface are constructive or destructive. Initial Level: Recognize changes (e.g., mountain formation, erosion, and glacial changes) that occurred on Earth's surface.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how internal and surface processes together formed a specific feature, such as the Zagros Mountains.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to show how Earth's internal and surface processes at different scales form continental and ocean-floor features.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can match landforms, such as mountains and trenches, to the plate movement that formed them, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name landforms such as mountains, valleys, and islands, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a model to show how volcanoes build up and weathering and erosion wear down Earth's surface.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.A Earth Materials and Systems, ESS2.D Weather and Climate)
text: Analyze geoscience data to make the claim that one change to Earth’s surface can create feedbacks that cause changes to other Earth systems.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze data to show a chain of feedbacks from one change, such as melting ice, and predict further effects.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze geoscience data to claim that one change to Earth's surface can create feedbacks that change other Earth systems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one change, like losing plants, affects another Earth system, using a cause-and-effect chart.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name Earth's systems: air, water, land, and living things, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.A Earth Materials and Systems, ESS2.B Plate Tectonics and Large-Scale System)
text: Develop a model based on evidence of Earth’s interior to describe the cycling of matter by thermal convection.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use seismic and heat evidence to model mantle convection and explain how it drives plate motion.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a model based on evidence of Earth's interior to describe how thermal convection cycles matter.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label Earth's layers and draw convection currents in the mantle, with a diagram guide.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name Earth's layers: crust, mantle, and core, using a model.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.A Earth Materials and Systems, ESS2.D Weather and Climate)
text: Use a model to describe how variations in the flow of energy into and out of Earth’s systems result in changes in climate.
ee_text: Target Level: Using a model, recognize how the effects of changes in climate can impact human lives. Precursor Level: Recognize climate changes have occurred (e.g., a change in average temperature, precipitation patterns, glacial ice volumes, sea levels). Initial Level: Recognize the differences between geographical climates (e.g., Minnesota versus Florida, desert versus rainforest).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how changes in energy flow, such as greenhouse gases or orbital changes, caused past and present climate change.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use a model to describe how changes in energy flowing into and out of Earth's systems change climate.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram of the greenhouse effect to explain why Earth warms, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun's energy warms Earth, using a picture.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a model to show how changes in climate can affect people's lives.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.C The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface)
text: Plan and conduct an investigation of the properties of water and its effects on Earth materials and surface processes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design and carry out an investigation of a property of water and explain how it causes weathering or erosion in the real world.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct an investigation of the properties of water and their effects on Earth materials and surface processes.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can follow a procedure to test how water affects rock or soil and record my observations, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that water can wear away rock and move soil, using a demonstration.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.D Weather and Climate)
text: Develop a quantitative model to describe the cycling of carbon among the hydrosphere, atmosphere, geosphere, and biosphere.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build a quantitative carbon model, use it to predict the effect of more emissions, and explain the limits of my model.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop a quantitative model to describe the cycling of carbon among the hydrosphere, atmosphere, geosphere, and biosphere.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use data to show where carbon is stored and how it moves between spheres, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name places where carbon is found, such as air, oceans, and living things.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.D Weather and Climate, ESS2.E Biogeology)
text: Construct an argument based on evidence about the simultaneous coevolution of Earth’s systems and life on Earth.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can argue with evidence how one change in life, such as photosynthesis, changed Earth's systems, and how those changes affected life.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an argument based on evidence about how Earth's systems and life on Earth have changed together over time.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one way living things changed Earth, such as plants adding oxygen to air, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that living things depend on air, water, and land, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.A Natural Resources, ESS3.B Natural Hazards)
text: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the availability of natural resources, occurrence of natural hazards, and changes in climate have influenced human activity.
ee_text: Target Level: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how natural hazards have influenced human activity. Precursor Level: Recognize how natural hazards (e.g., floods, earthquakes, tornadoes) influence human activity. Initial Level: Recognize characteristics of natural hazards (e.g., floods, earthquakes, tornadoes).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how resources, hazards, and climate shaped human settlement in a region, such as the history of Qatar.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how natural resources, natural hazards, and climate change have influenced human activity.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one resource or hazard affected where people live, using a case study and sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people live near water and other resources, using maps or pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can explain with evidence how natural hazards have changed how people live.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.A Natural Resources)
text: Evaluate competing design solutions for developing, managing, and utilizing energy and mineral resources based on cost-benefit ratios.
ee_text: Target Level: Construct an argument for a strategy to conserve, recycle, or reuse resources. Precursor Level: Describe the factors that would favor one strategy to conserve, recycle, or reuse resources over another. Initial Level: Recognize strategies to manage objects (e.g., dispose, repurpose, or recycle).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate several energy or mineral resource solutions with cost-benefit data and recommend the best one with reasons.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate competing design solutions for developing, managing, and using energy and mineral resources based on cost-benefit ratios.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare two energy sources, such as solar and natural gas, using a pros and cons table.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort energy sources into renewable and nonrenewable, using pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can argue for a way to conserve, recycle, or reuse a resource.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.C Human Impacts on Earth Systems)
text: Create a computational simulation to illustrate the relationships among the management of natural resources, the sustainability of human populations, and biodiversity.
ee_text: Target Level: Analyze data to determine the effects of a conservation strategy on the level of a natural resource. Precursor Level: Organize data on the effects of conservation strategies (e.g., using less energy, using rechargeable batteries, recycling or repurposing materials). Initial Level: Gather data on the effects of a local (e.g., class or school-wide) conservation strategy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build and run a simulation, test management choices, and explain how they affect people and biodiversity over time.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create a computational simulation to show relationships among natural resource management, sustainability of human populations, and biodiversity.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a given simulation and change one management choice to see its effect, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that using too many resources can harm people and nature, using examples.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use data to tell how a conservation plan changed the amount of a natural resource.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.C Human Impacts on Earth Systems)
text: Evaluate or refine a technological solution that reduces impacts of human activities on natural systems.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate and refine a technology, such as desalination or carbon capture, using data on costs, benefits, and environmental impact.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate or refine a technological solution that reduces impacts of human activities on natural systems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one technology reduces a human impact and list one benefit and one drawback, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name technologies that help the environment, such as recycling machines or solar panels.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.D Global Climate Change)
text: Analyze geoscience data and the results from global climate models to make an evidence-based forecast of the current rate of global or regional climate change and associated future impacts to Earth’s systems.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze climate model results and data to forecast regional change, such as in the Gulf, and explain the uncertainty in my forecast.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze geoscience data and climate model results to make an evidence-based forecast of climate change and its future impacts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a temperature graph and describe the trend and one likely impact, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth's average temperature is rising, using a simple graph.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.D Global Climate Change)
text: Use a computational representation to illustrate the relationships among Earth systems and how those relationships are being modified due to human activity.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a computational model to show how a human activity changes several linked Earth systems and test a way to reduce the change.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use a computational representation to show relationships among Earth systems and how human activity is changing them.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a given model or graph to describe how a human activity changes one Earth system, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name ways people change the air, water, and land, using pictures.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.A Defining Engineering Problems)
text: Analyze a major global challenge to specify qualitative and quantitative criteria and constraints for solutions that account for societal needs and wants.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze a global challenge, such as water scarcity, and write precise, measurable criteria and constraints that reflect different societal needs.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze a major global challenge to specify qualitative and quantitative criteria and constraints that account for societal needs and wants.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a global problem and list some criteria and constraints for a solution, using a template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a big world problem, such as clean water, with support.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.C Optimizing the Design Solution)
text: Design a solution to a complex real-world problem by breaking it down into smaller, more manageable problems that can be solved through engineering.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can break a complex problem into smaller problems, design solutions for each, and explain how they work together.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can design a solution to a complex real-world problem by breaking it into smaller problems that can be solved through engineering.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can break a problem into two or three smaller parts and suggest a solution for one part, with a graphic organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe a problem and one idea to solve it, with support.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions)
text: Evaluate a solution to a complex real-world problem based on prioritized criteria and trade-offs that account for a range of constraints, including cost, safety, reliability, and aesthetics, as well as possible social, cultural, and environmental impacts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate several solutions using prioritized criteria and trade-offs and justify my choice, including social, cultural, and environmental impacts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate a solution to a complex problem using prioritized criteria and trade-offs, including cost, safety, reliability, aesthetics, and social and environmental impacts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a decision matrix to rate a solution against given criteria, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say one good thing and one problem with a solution, using sentence frames.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions)
text: Use a computer simulation to model the impact of proposed solutions to a complex real-world problem with numerous criteria and constraints on interactions within and between systems relevant to the problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build or modify a computer simulation, test several solutions, and explain how the results show interactions between systems.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use a computer simulation to model how proposed solutions to a complex problem affect interactions within and between systems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can run a given simulation with two solutions and compare the results, with step-by-step support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use a simple simulation and describe what happens when I change one thing, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
text: Plan and conduct an investigation to compare the effects of different strengths or different directions of pushes and pulls on the motion of an object.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design and carry out an investigation to compare how different strengths of pushes and pulls affect the motion of various objects. Example: I can push a light ball and a heavy ball, explaining which one rolls farther and why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct a simple investigation to see how different pushes affect the motion of an object. Example: I can test how far a car rolls with a soft push compared to a hard push.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how pushing or pulling changes where an object goes. Example: I can say that pulling my toy closer makes it stop moving away.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that some objects move when I push or pull them. Example: I can point to a toy and say it rolls when I push it.

source: AERO Science PK-5 Framework Progressions Matrix (school copy)

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
text: Analyze data to determine if a design solution works as intended to change the speed or direction of an object with a push or a pull.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design an experiment to show how balanced and unbalanced forces work in real life, explaining my observations. Example: I can demonstrate using a seesaw to explain how weight affects balance and movement.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can conduct an investigation to explore how balanced and unbalanced forces affect the motion of an object. Example: I can push two toy cars at the same time and see one move while the other stays still.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe when an object moves and when it doesn’t based on how I push or pull it. Example: I can explain that my toy car moves when I push it hard but not when I just touch it.
descriptors.cc_emerging: can see that some objects do not move when I push or pull them. Example: I can say that a heavy box stays in place when I try to push it.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can test a ramp or other tool, use my results to explain how it changes an object's speed or direction, and make it work better.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can look at test results to tell if my design, like a ramp, changes the speed or direction of an object as I wanted.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can test a ramp with a ball and say if the ball went faster or changed direction, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can push a ball and show that it can go fast, slow, or turn.

source: AERO Science PK-5 Framework Progressions Matrix (school copy)

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy
text: Make observations to determine the effect of sunlight on Earth’s surface.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design a simple project to demonstrate energy transfer in action and explain what happens. Example: I can create a simple circuit with a battery and a light bulb and describe how the energy makes the bulb light up.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can observe and explain how energy can be transferred from one object to another. Example: I can show how rubbing my hands together creates heat.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how energy is used in everyday objects. Example: I can explain that a toy car needs batteries to move.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that some things can make light or sound. Example: I can say that a flashlight makes light when I turn it on.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can compare how warm different surfaces get in the sun, such as sand, water, and grass, and explain why.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can make observations to tell how sunlight changes Earth's surface, such as making sand or water warmer.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can touch things in the sun and in the shade and say which is warmer, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun makes things feel warm.

source: AERO Science PK-5 Framework Progressions Matrix (school copy)

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy
text: Use tools and materials provided to design and build a structure that will reduce the warming effect of sunlight on Earth’s surface.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design and build a sunshade and explain how it works in real life to keep things cool. Example: I create a sunshade and share my ideas about how it could help people or animals stay safe from the sun.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use tools and materials to design and build a sunshade that keeps things cool in the sun. Example: I create a sunshade with a clear structure and explain how it helps reduce heat.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can choose some materials and start to build my sunshade with help. Example: I use cardboard and tape to make a simple shape but need support to finish it.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what I want to make but need help with my ideas. Example: I can tell someone I want to build a shade but don’t know how.

source: AERO Science PK-5 Framework Progressions Matrix (school copy)

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
text: Use observations to describe patterns of what plants and animals (including humans) need to survive.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can investigate and explain how different environments meet the needs of various plants and animals. Example: I can compare how a cactus and a tree get water and explain why they need different amounts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and explain the basic needs of plants and animals, including food, water, and shelter. Example: I can list that plants need sunlight, water, and soil to grow.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what plants and animals need to live and grow. Example: I can explain that animals need food and water.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize that living things need certain things to grow. Example: I can say that plants need water.

source: AERO Science PK-5 Framework Progressions Matrix (school copy)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems
text: Use and share observation s of local weather conditions to describe patterns over time.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can investigate and explain how different weather patterns impact the environment and living things.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can observe and report on daily weather conditions and how they affect my surroundings. Example: I can tell what the weather is like today and how it affects my playtime outside.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some local places, but I struggle to explain their purposes. Example: I can name a park, but I don’t know what activities happen there.

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can make a detailed model or map of land and water in an area and explain what it shows.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can make a model to show the shapes and kinds of land and bodies of water in an area.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can label land and water features, like hills and the sea, on a model with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can point to land and water on a map or picture.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems
text: Obtain information to identify where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of family roles to suggest ways to strengthen family relationships. Example: I can propose having regular family game nights to help us bond and have fun together.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the roles of various family members and give specific examples of how they contribute to the family. Example: I can explain that parents provide care and guidance, helping us learn and grow.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some family roles and mention their responsibilities, but my explanations are basic. Example: I can say that a sibling plays with me, but I can’t explain how we support each other.

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can find where water is on Earth in different forms and explain which places have solid or liquid water.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can get information to tell where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can name places with water, like oceans and ice, using pictures with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can say that water can be ice or liquid.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design
text: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change to define a simple problem that can be solved through the development of a new or improved object or tool.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can investigate and create a simple design to solve a problem, and explain how it works. Example: I can build a model of a windmill and explain how it can help generate energy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify a problem, plan a solution, and explain my design. Example: I can say that we need a way to keep drinks cold and describe how I would design a cooler.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design
text: Analyze data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of how each performs.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can identify a problem, ask detailed questions, and suggest ways to create or improve an object or tool to solve it. Example: I see that my bike is hard to ride and propose making a new seat that is more comfortable.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask questions and gather information to define a simple problem that needs a new or better tool. Example: I observe that a toy is hard to play with and say, "We need a new way to hold it."
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask questions and make observations about a problem that needs fixing. Example: I notice that my backpack is heavy and ask, "How can I make it easier to carry?"
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can ask basic questions about a problem but need help understanding it. Example: I might ask, "Why is it hard to carry things?" but don't know how to solve it.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can test two designs, record results in a chart, and explain which is stronger and why.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can look at test results from two objects made to solve the same problem and compare what each does well and not well.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can test two designs and say which one worked better, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can watch two designs being tested and point to the one that worked.
