subject: Science
cluster: SEP1.A: Asking Questions
text: Students ask questions to specify relationships between variables and clarify arguments and models. This includes the following: Ask questions that arise from careful observation of phenomena, models, or unexpected results to clarify or seek additional information. Ask questions to identify and clarify evidence and the premise(s) of an argument. Ask questions to determine relationships between independent and dependent variables and relationships in models. Ask questions to clarify or refine a model, an explanation, or an engineering problem. Ask questions that require sufficient and appropriate empirical evidence to answer. Ask questions that can be investigated within the scope of the classroom, outdoor environment, and museums and other public facilities with available resources and, when appropriate, frame a hypothesis based on observations and scientific principles. Ask questions that challenge the premise(s) of an argument or the interpretation of a data set.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask questions that clarify a model or argument and refine them into testable research questions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask questions that specify relationships between variables and clarify arguments and models.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask a testable question with an independent and dependent variable, using a template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can ask a question about an observation, using question starters.

cluster: SEP2: Developing and Using Models
text: Students use, synthesize, and develop models to predict and show relationships among variables and between systems and their components in the natural and designed world. This includes the following: With guidance, plan and conduct an investigation in collaboration with peers (for K). Plan and conduct an investigation collaboratively to produce data to serve as the basis for evidence to answer a question. Evaluate different ways of observing and measuring a phenomenon to determine which way can answer the question being studied. Make observations (firsthand or from media) and measurements to collect data that can be used to make comparisons. Make observations (firsthand or from media) and measurements of a proposed object or tool or solution to determine if it solves a problem or meets a goal.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can plan a fair test with a partner, make careful observations, and use data to answer my question.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and carry out simple investigations, based on fair tests, with peers, and make observations to collect data.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can follow steps to carry out an investigation and record what I see, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can observe an investigation and share one thing I noticed.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP3: Planning and Conducting Investigations
text: Students plan and carry out investigations that control variables and provide evidence to support explanations or design solutions. This includes the following: Collaboratively plan and conduct an investigation to produce data to serve as the basis for evidence, using fair tests in which variables are controlled and the number of trials considered. Evaluate appropriate methods and tools for collecting data. Make observations and measurements to produce data to serve as the basis for evidence for an explanation of a phenomenon or test a design solution. Make predictions about what would happen if a variable changes. Test two different models of the same proposed object, tool, or process to determine which better meets criteria for success.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can plan and carry out a fair test, control variables, and run several trials to produce reliable evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and carry out investigations that control variables and give evidence to support explanations or design solutions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can follow a plan for a fair test and record measurements, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can carry out simple steps of an investigation, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP3: Planning and Conducting Investigations
text: Students plan and carry out investigations that use multiple variables and provide evidence to support explanations or solutions. This includes the following: Individually and collaboratively plan an investigation, identifying: independent and dependent variables and controls, tools needed to do the gathering, how measurements will be recorded, and how many data are needed to support a claim. Conduct an investigation. Evaluate and revise the experimental design to produce data that serve as the basis for evidence to meet the goals of the investigation. Evaluate the accuracy of various methods for collecting data. Collect data under a range of conditions that serve as the basis for evidence to answer scientific questions or test design solutions. Collect data about the performance of a proposed object, tool, process, or system under a range of conditions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can plan an investigation with independent and dependent variables and controls, collect accurate data, and evaluate my method.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and carry out investigations with multiple variables that provide evidence for explanations or solutions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the variables in an investigation and collect data, with a planning template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can follow a lab procedure safely and record data, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP3: Planning and Conducting Investigations
text: Students plan and carry out investigations that provide evidence for and test conceptual, mathematical, physical, and empirical models: This includes the following: Individually and collaboratively plan an investigation or test a design to produce data that can serve as evidence to build and revise models, support explanations for phenomena, and refine solutions to problems. Consider possible variables or effects and evaluate the investigation’s design to ensure variables are controlled. Individually and collaboratively plan and conduct an investigation to produce data to serve as the basis for evidence. In the design, decide on types, how much, and accuracy of data needed to produce reliable measurements. Consider limitations on the precision of the data (e.g., number of trials, cost, risk, time) and refine the design accordingly. Plan and conduct an investigation or test a design solution in a safe and ethical manner including considerations of environmental, social, and personal impacts. Select appropriate tools to collect, record, analyze, and evaluate data. Make directional hypotheses that specify what happens to a dependent variable when an independent variable is manipulated. Manipulate variables and collect data about a complex model of a proposed process or system to identify failure points, or to improve performance relative to criteria for success.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design an investigation, decide the data and precision needed, and use results to revise a model.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and carry out investigations that give evidence to build and test conceptual, mathematical, physical, and empirical models.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can plan an investigation with variables and controls, using a template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can follow a lab procedure and record data accurately, with support.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP4: Analyzing and Interpreting Data
text: Students collect, record, and share observations. This includes the following: Record information (observations, thoughts, and ideas). Use and share pictures, drawings, or writings of observations. Use observations (firsthand or from media) to describe patterns or relationships in the natural and designed worlds in order to answer scientific questions and solve problems. Compare predictions (based on prior experiences) to what occurred (observable events). Analyze data from tests of an object or tool to determine if the object or tool works as intended.

descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw or record what I observe, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell a partner what I see.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP4: Analyzing and Interpreting Data
text: Students begin to use quantitative approaches to collect data and conduct multiple trials of qualitative observations. (When possible, digital tools should be used.) This includes the following: Represent data in tables or various graphical displays (bar graphs, pictographs, and pie charts) to reveal patterns that indicate relationships. Analyze and interpret data to make sense of phenomena, using logical reasoning, mathematics, or computation. Compare and contrast data collected by different groups in order to discuss similarities and differences in their findings. Analyze data to refine a problem statement or the design of a proposed object, tool, or process. Use data to evaluate and refine design solutions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose the best graph for my data and use it to explain a pattern and refine a design.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can collect data, show it in tables and graphs, and analyze it to reveal patterns.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can put data into a table or bar graph, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can read one value from a simple table or graph, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP4: Analyzing and Interpreting Data
text: Students extend quantitative analysis to investigations, distinguishing between correlation and causation, and basic statistical techniques of data and error analysis. This includes the following: Construct, analyze, or interpret graphical displays of data and large data sets to identify linear and nonlinear relationships. Use graphical displays (e.g., maps, charts, graphs, and tables) of large data sets to identify temporal and spatial relationships. Distinguish between causal and correlational relationships in data. Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence for explanations of phenomena. Apply concepts of statistics and probability (including mean, median, mode, and variability) to analyze and characterize data, using digital tools when feasible. Consider limitations of data analysis (e.g., measurement error), and seek to improve precision and accuracy of data with better technological tools and methods (e.g., multiple trials). Analyze and interpret data to determine similarities and differences in findings. Analyze data to define an optimal operational range for a proposed object, tool, process, or system that best meets criteria for success.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze large data sets, tell correlation from causation, and use error analysis to judge my results.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct and interpret graphs and data sets to find relationships, telling correlation from causation and using basic statistics.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can make a graph and describe the trend it shows, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can read values from a graph or table, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP4: Analyzing and Interpreting Data
text: Students engage in more detailed statistical analysis, the comparison of data sets for consistency, and the use of models to generate and analyze data. This includes the following: Analyze data using tools, technologies, and models (e.g., computational, mathematical) in order to make valid and reliable scientific claims or determine an optimal design solution. Apply concepts of statistics and probability to scientific and engineering questions and problems, using digital tools when feasible. Concepts should include determining the fit of functions, slope, and intercepts to data, along with correlation coefficients when the data is linear. Consider and address more sophisticated limitations of data analysis (e.g., sample selection) when analyzing and interpreting data. Compare and contrast various types of data sets (e.g., self-generated, archival) to examine consistency of measurements and observations. Evaluate the impact of new data on a working explanation or model of a proposed process or system. Analyze data to optimize design features or characteristics of system components relative to criteria for success.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use statistics and models to compare data sets, judge consistency, and optimize a design.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze data using tools and models, compare data sets for consistency, and make valid and reliable claims.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can analyze a data set for trends and outliers, with guided steps.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can make a graph from data and describe it, with support.

This includes the following: Use counting and numbers to identify and describe patterns in the natural and designed worlds. Describe, measure, or compare quantitative attributes of different objects and display the data using simple graphs. Use qualitative and/or quantitative data to compare two alternative solutions to a problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use counting and measuring to compare objects and display data to answer a question.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use counting and numbers to describe patterns and measure and compare attributes of objects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can count objects and say which group has more, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can count objects in a group.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP5: Using Mathematics and Computational Thinking
text: Students extend quantitative measurements to a variety of physical properties, using computation and mathematics to analyze data and compare alternative design solutions. This includes the following: Organize simple data sets to reveal patterns that suggest relationships. Describe, measure, estimate, and/or graph quantities such as area, volume, weight, and time to address scientific and engineering questions and problems. Create and use graphs or charts generated from simple algorithms to compare alternative solutions to an engineering problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use math to analyze data and compare design solutions, explaining which is best.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can measure physical properties and use math to organize data, find patterns, and compare design solutions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can measure and record quantities and find a simple total or difference, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can measure with a tool and write the number, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP5: Using Mathematics and Computational Thinking
text: Students identify patterns in large data sets and use mathematical concepts to support explanations and arguments. This includes the following: Decide when to use qualitative vs. quantitative data. Use digital tools (e.g., computers) to analyze very large data sets for patterns and trends. Use mathematical representations to describe and support scientific conclusions and design solutions. Create algorithms (a series of ordered steps) to solve a problem. Apply mathematical concepts and processes (such as ratio, rate, percent, basic operations, and simple algebra) to scientific and engineering questions and problems. Use digital tools and mathematical concepts and arguments to test and compare proposed solutions to an engineering design problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use digital tools and math to find trends in large data sets and use them to support an argument.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can find patterns in large data sets and use math concepts such as ratio and rate to support explanations and arguments.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can calculate a rate or ratio from data, with a worked example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can do a simple calculation with data, with support.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP5: Using Mathematics and Computational Thinking
text: Students use algebraic thinking and analysis, a range of linear and nonlinear functions (including trigonometric functions, exponentials, and logarithms), and computational tools for statistical analysis to analyze, represent, and model data. Simple computational simulations are created and used based on mathematical models of basic assumptions. This includes the following: Decide if qualitative or quantitative data are best to determine whether a proposed object or tool meets criteria for success. Create and/or revise a computational model or simulation of a phenomenon, designed device, process, or system. Use mathematical, computational, and algorithmic representations of phenomena or design solutions to describe and support claims and explanations. Apply techniques of algebra and functions to represent and solve scientific and engineering problems. Use simple limit cases to test mathematical expressions, computer programs, algorithms, or simulations of a process or system to see if a model “makes sense” by comparing the outcomes with what is known about the real world. Apply ratios, rates, percentages, and unit conversions in the context of complicated measurement problems involving quantities with derived or compound units (such as mg/mL, kg/m3, acre-feet, and others).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create a computational simulation from math models and use it to test a claim or design.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use algebra, functions, and computational tools to analyze, represent, and model data.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use an equation to calculate values from data, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can substitute values into a given formula, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP6.A: Constructing an Explanation
text: Students use evidence and ideas in constructing evidence-based accounts of natural phenomena. This includes the following: Use information from observations (firsthand and from media) to construct an evidence-based account for natural phenomena.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain what happened using evidence from several observations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use observations to make an evidence-based account of a natural event.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell what happened and give one observation as evidence, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe what I saw happen.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP6.A: Constructing an Explanation
text: Students use evidence to construct explanations that specify variables that describe and predict phenomena. This includes the following: Construct an explanation of observed relationships (e.g., the distribution of plants in the back yard). Use evidence (e.g., measurements, observations, patterns) to construct or support an explanation. Identify the evidence that supports particular points in an explanation.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use evidence to explain a phenomenon and predict what will happen if a variable changes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use evidence such as measurements and patterns to construct explanations that describe and predict phenomena.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write an explanation with one piece of evidence, using a claim-evidence frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what I think happened and why, with support.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP6.A: Constructing an Explanation
text: Students construct explanations supported by multiple sources of evidence consistent with scientific ideas, principles, and theories. This includes the following: Construct an explanation that includes qualitative or quantitative relationships between variables that predict and describe phenomena. Construct an explanation using models or representations. Construct a scientific explanation based on valid and reliable evidence obtained from sources, including the students’ own experiments. Solutions should build on the following assumption: Theories and laws that describe the natural world operate today as they did in the past and will continue to do so in the future. Apply scientific ideas, principles, and evidence to construct, revise, or use an explanation for real world phenomena, examples, or events.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can construct an explanation using several sources of evidence and scientific reasoning and apply it to a new situation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct explanations supported by multiple sources of evidence that are consistent with scientific ideas and theories.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a claim, evidence, and reasoning explanation, using a template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can make a claim and give one piece of evidence, using sentence frames.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP6.A: Constructing an Explanation
text: Students create explanations that are supported by multiple and independent student-generated sources of evidence consistent with scientific ideas, principles, and theories. This includes the following: Make quantitative and qualitative claims regarding the relationship between dependent and independent variables. Construct and revise an explanation based on valid and reliable evidence obtained from a variety of sources, including students’ own investigations, models, theories, simulations, and peer review. Explanations should reflect the assumption that theories and laws that describe the natural world operate today as they did in the past and will continue to do so in the future. Apply scientific ideas, principles, and evidence to provide an explanation of phenomena taking into account possible, unanticipated effects. Apply scientific reasoning, theory, and models to link evidence to the claim and to assess the extent to which the reasoning and data support the explanation.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can construct and revise an explanation using independent evidence I generated and theories, and judge its limits.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create explanations supported by multiple independent sources of my own evidence and consistent with scientific ideas and theories.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a claim, evidence, and reasoning explanation using data, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can make a claim and support it with one piece of evidence, with sentence frames.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP7: Arguing from Evidence
text: Students compare ideas and representations about the natural and designed world. This includes the following: Identify arguments that are supported by evidence. Distinguish between explanations that account for all gathered evidence and those that do not. Analyze why some evidence is relevant to a scientific question and some is not. Distinguish between opinions and evidence in one’s own explanations. Listen actively to arguments to indicate agreement or disagreement based on evidence, or to retell the main points of the argument. Construct an argument with evidence to support a claim. Make a claim about the effectiveness of an object, tool, or solution that is supported by relevant evidence.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can make a claim, support it with evidence, and explain why some evidence is better than other evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compare ideas, identify arguments supported by evidence, and construct an argument with evidence to support a claim.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can make a claim and give one reason, using a sentence frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say whether I agree or disagree with an idea.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP7: Arguing from Evidence
text: Students critique the scientific explanations or solutions proposed by peers by citing relevant evidence about the natural and designed world. This includes the following: Compare and refine arguments based on an evaluation of the evidence presented. Distinguish among facts, reasoned judgment based on research findings, and speculation in an explanation. Respectfully provide and receive critiques from peers about a proposed procedure, explanation, or model by citing relevant evidence and posing specific questions. Construct and/or support an argument with evidence, data, or a model. Use data to evaluate claims about cause and effect. Make a claim about the merit of a solution to a problem by citing relevant evidence about how it meets the criteria and constraints of the problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can critique a peer's explanation with evidence and improve my own argument based on feedback.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can critique explanations or solutions proposed by peers by citing relevant evidence and construct arguments with evidence, data, or a model.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can make a claim and share one reason, with support.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP7: Arguing from Evidence
text: Students construct a convincing argument that supports or refutes claims for either explanations or solutions about the natural and designed world. This includes the following. Compare and critique two arguments on the same topic. Analyze whether they emphasize similar or different evidence and interpretations of facts. Respectfully provide and receive critiques about one’s explanations, procedures, models, and questions by citing relevant evidence and posing and responding to questions that elicit pertinent elaboration and detail. Construct, use, and present oral and written arguments supported by empirical evidence and scientific reasoning to support or refute an explanation or a model for a phenomenon or a solution to a problem. Make an oral or written argument that supports or refutes the advertised performance of a device, process, or system. Based the argument on empirical evidence concerning whether or not the technology meets relevant criteria and constraints. Evaluate competing design solutions based on jointly developed and agreed-upon design criteria.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare and critique two arguments and construct a convincing written and oral argument with empirical evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct a convincing argument that supports or refutes claims for explanations or solutions, using evidence and reasoning.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write an argument with a claim, evidence, and reasoning, using a template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can state a claim and one piece of evidence, using sentence frames.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP7: Arguing from Evidence
text: Students use appropriate and sufficient evidence and scientific reasoning to defend and critique claims and explanations about the natural and designed world. Arguments may also come from current scientific or historical episodes in science. This includes the following: Compare and evaluate competing arguments or design solutions in light of currently accepted explanations, new evidence, limitations (e.g., trade-offs), constraints, and ethical issues. Evaluate the claims, evidence, and reasoning behind currently accepted explanations or solutions to determine the merits of arguments. Respectfully provide and receive critiques on scientific arguments by probing reasoning and evidence, by challenging ideas and conclusions, by responding thoughtfully to diverse perspectives, and by determining what additional information is required to resolve contradictions. Construct, use, and present oral and written arguments or counter-arguments based on data and evidence. Make and defend a claim based on evidence about the natural world or the effectiveness of a design solution that reflects scientific knowledge and student-generated evidence. Evaluate competing design solutions to a real-world problem based on scientific ideas and principles, empirical evidence, and logical arguments. Consider relevant factors (e.g. economic, societal, environmental, and ethical considerations).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate competing arguments from science history or current issues and respectfully critique reasoning and evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use appropriate and sufficient evidence and scientific reasoning to defend and critique claims and explanations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can defend a claim with evidence and respond to one counterargument, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can state a claim and give evidence for it, using sentence frames.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP8: Obtaining, Evaluating, and Communicating Information
text: Students use observations and texts to communicate new information. This includes the following: Read developmentally appropriate texts or use media to obtain scientific and technical information. Use the information to determine patterns in or evidence about the natural and designed worlds. Describe how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) support a scientific or engineering idea. Obtain information using various texts, text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons), and other media that will be useful in answering scientific questions or supporting scientific claims. Communicate information or design ideas and solutions with others in oral or written forms. Use models, drawings, writing, or numbers that provide detail about scientific ideas, practices, or design ideas.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can find information in texts and media, describe how it answers my question, and share it in several ways.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can read texts or use media to get science information, use it to find patterns or evidence, and communicate it.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find one fact in a picture book or video and share it, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can look at pictures in a book and say what I learned.

cluster: SEP8: Obtaining, Evaluating, and Communicating Information
text: Students evaluate the merit and accuracy of ideas and methods. Gather, read, and synthesize information from multiple appropriate sources and assess the credibility, accuracy, and possible bias of each publication. Describe how they are supported or not supported by evidence and evaluate methods used. Evaluate data, hypotheses, and conclusions in scientific and technical texts in light of competing information or accounts. Communicate scientific and technical information (e.g. about a proposed object, tool, process, or system) in writing and through oral presentations.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the credibility of several sources, synthesize their information, and present it clearly to an audience.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can critically read science texts, evaluate the merit of ideas and methods, and communicate information in several formats.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the central idea of a science text and summarize it, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find key words and facts in a science text, with a word bank.

subject: Science
cluster: SEP8: Obtaining, Evaluating, and Communicating Information
text: Students evaluate the validity and reliability of claims, methods, and designs. This includes the following: Critically read scientific literature adapted for classroom use to determine the central ideas or conclusions, and to obtain scientific and technical information. Summarize complex evidence, concepts, processes, or information presented in a text by paraphrasing them in simpler but still accurate terms. Compare, integrate, and evaluate sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, or text-based) in order to address a scientific question or solve a problem. Gather, read, and evaluate scientific and technical information from multiple authoritative sources, assessing the evidence and usefulness of each source. Synthesize and evaluate the validity and reliability of multiple claims, methods, or designs that appear in scientific and technical texts or media reports. Verify the data when possible. Communicate scientific and technical information in multiple formats, including orally, graphically, textually, and mathematically. Examples of information could include ideas about phenomena or the design and performance of a proposed process or system.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can critically read scientific literature, evaluate competing claims, and communicate complex information in multiple formats.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate the validity and reliability of claims, methods, and designs and communicate scientific information in multiple formats.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can summarize evidence from a scientific text and say if the source is reliable, with guided questions.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the main idea of a scientific text, with support.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.A: Structure and Function
text: All organisms have external parts that they use to perform daily functions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare external parts of several plants and animals and explain how each part helps in daily life.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe how organisms use their external parts to do daily functions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name an external part of a plant or animal and say what it does, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to parts of a plant or animal, such as leaves, legs, or wings.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.A: Structure and Function
text: Plants and animals have both internal and external macroscopic structures that allow for growth, survival, behavior, and reproduction.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how internal and external structures work together to help an organism survive and reproduce.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants and animals have internal and external structures for growth, survival, behavior, and reproduction.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name an internal or external structure and its job, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name body parts of animals and parts of plants, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.A: Structure and Function
text: All living things are made up of cells. In organisms, cells work together to form tissues and organs that are specialized for particular body functions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how cells, tissues, and organs work together in a body system using an example.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that living things are made of cells that form tissues and organs specialized for body functions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can put cells, tissues, and organs in order of size, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that living things are made of cells.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.A: Structure and Function
text: Systems of specialized cells within organisms help perform essential functions of life. Any one system in an organism is made up of numerous parts. Feedback mechanisms maintain an organism’s internal conditions within certain limits and mediate behaviors.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how specialized cell systems and feedback keep an organism's internal conditions stable in a new situation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how systems of specialized cells perform life functions and how feedback maintains internal conditions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one body system and one feedback example, such as sweating, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name body systems and organs, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.B: Growth and Development of Organisms
text: Parents and offspring often engage in behaviors that help the offspring survive.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare how different parents and offspring behave and explain how each behavior helps survival.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe behaviors of parents and offspring that help the offspring survive.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one example of a parent animal caring for its young, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match baby animals to their parents, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.B: Growth and Development of Organisms
text: Reproduction is essential to every kind of organism. Organisms have unique and diverse life cycles.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare life cycles of different organisms and explain what all life cycles have in common.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that reproduction is essential and that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can put the stages of one life cycle in order, with picture cards.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that living things are born and grow, using pictures.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.B: Growth and Development of Organisms
text: Animals engage in behaviors that increase the odds of reproduction. An organism’s growth is affected by both genetic and environmental factors.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use evidence to explain how behaviors, genes, and environment together affect reproduction and growth.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how animal behaviors increase reproduction and how genetic and environmental factors affect growth.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give an example of a behavior that helps reproduction and a factor that affects growth, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that living things need food and water to grow.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.B: Growth and Development of Organisms
text: Growth and division of cells in organisms occurs by mitosis and differentiation for specific cell types.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how mitosis and differentiation produce different cell types and what happens when this goes wrong.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that cells grow and divide by mitosis and differentiate into specific cell types.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the stages of mitosis using a diagram, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that cells divide to make new cells.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.C: Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in Organisms
text: Animals obtain food they need from plants or other animals. Plants need water and light.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain and compare what different plants and animals need for food and energy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can say that animals get food from plants or other animals and that plants need water and light.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort animals by what they eat, with picture cards.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that animals eat and plants need water.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.C: Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in Organisms
text: Food provides animals with the materials and energy they need for body repair, growth, warmth, and motion. Plants acquire material for growth chiefly from air, water, and process matter, and obtain energy from sunlight, which is used to maintain conditions necessary for survival.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how plants get most of their material from air and water and how this energy reaches animals.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that food gives animals materials and energy and that plants get material mainly from air and water and energy from sunlight.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what plants and animals need to grow, using a diagram and word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants need sunlight and animals need food.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.C: Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in Organisms
text: Plants use the energy from light to make sugars through photosynthesis. Within individual organisms, food is broken down through a series of chemical reactions that rearrange molecules and release energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can trace energy from sunlight through photosynthesis into food and explain how cells release it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants use light energy to make sugars and that food is broken down in organisms to release energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the inputs and outputs of photosynthesis, using a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants make food using sunlight.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.C: Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in Organisms
text: The molecules produced through photosynthesis are used to make amino acids and other molecules that can be assembled into proteins or DNA. Through cellular respiration, matter and energy flow through different organizational levels of an organism as elements are recombined to form different products and transfer energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can trace atoms and energy from photosynthesis through cellular respiration and into proteins and DNA.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how molecules from photosynthesis build proteins and DNA and how respiration moves matter and energy through an organism.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how photosynthesis and respiration are linked, using a diagram with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the inputs of photosynthesis and respiration, with a word bank.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.D: Information Processing
text: Animals sense and communicate information and respond to inputs with behaviors that help them grow and survive.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how animals use several senses and signals to respond and survive, with examples.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe how animals sense, communicate, and respond with behaviors that help them grow and survive.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give an example of an animal responding to something it senses, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the senses animals use, such as seeing and hearing.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.D: Information Processing
text: Different sense receptors are specialized for particular kinds of information; animals use their perceptions and memories to guide their actions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can model how different senses send information to the brain and how memory guides an animal's actions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that sense receptors detect different information and animals use perceptions and memories to guide actions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can match a sense organ to the information it detects, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the five senses and their body parts.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.D: Information Processing
text: Each sense receptor responds to different inputs, transmitting them as signals that travel along nerve cells to the brain. The signals are then processed in the brain resulting in immediate behavior or memories.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain the full pathway from sense receptor to brain and compare a reflex with a memory.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that sense receptors send signals along nerve cells to the brain, which leads to behavior or memories.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw the path from a sense organ to the brain, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that the brain receives messages from the senses.

subject: Science
cluster: LS1.D: Information Processing
text: Organisms can process and store a variety of information through specific chemicals and interconnected networks.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how chemical signals and nerve networks process and store information, using an example such as learning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that organisms process and store information through specific chemicals and interconnected networks.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe that nerves and hormones carry messages in the body, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that the brain and nerves help us respond.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.A: Interdependent Relationships in Ecosystems
text: Plants depend on water and light to grow. Plants depend on animals for pollination or to move their seeds around.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how plants and animals depend on each other, using examples of pollination and seed dispersal.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants need water and light and depend on animals for pollination or to move seeds.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how a bee or bird helps a plant, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants need water and sunlight.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.A: Interdependent Relationships in Ecosystems
text: The food of almost any animal can be traced back to plants. Organisms are related in food webs in which some animals eat plants for food and other animals eat the animals that eat plants, while decomposers restore some materials back to the soil.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build a food web and explain how energy from plants reaches all animals and how decomposers recycle materials.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that animals' food traces back to plants and that food webs include producers, consumers, and decomposers.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can build a simple food chain starting with a plant, using picture cards.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what some animals eat.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.A: Interdependent Relationships in Ecosystems
text: Organisms and populations are dependent on their environmental interactions both with other living things and with nonliving factors, any of which can limit their growth. Competitive, predatory, and mutually beneficial interactions vary across ecosystems but the patterns are shared.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict how changing a living or nonliving factor will affect several populations in an ecosystem.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that organisms depend on living and nonliving factors, which can limit growth, and describe competitive, predatory, and helpful interactions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify predator, prey, and competition in an ecosystem, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name living and nonliving things in an ecosystem.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.A: Interdependent Relationships in Ecosystems
text: Ecosystems have carrying capacities resulting from biotic and abiotic factors. The fundamental tension between resource availability and organism populations affects the abundance of species in any given ecosystem. The combination of the factors that affect an organism's success can be measured as a multidimensional niche.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use data to explain how biotic and abiotic factors set carrying capacity and predict population changes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that ecosystems have carrying capacities set by biotic and abiotic factors that affect species abundance.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a population graph and identify carrying capacity, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that ecosystems have limited food and space.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.B: Cycles of Matter and Energy Transfer in Ecosystems
text: Matter cycles between the air and soil and among organisms as they live and die.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can model how matter moves between air, soil, and living things and explain the role of decomposers.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that matter cycles between air, soil, and organisms as they live and die.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what happens to a dead plant in soil, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that dead leaves break down into soil.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.B: Cycles of Matter and Energy Transfer in Ecosystems
text: The atoms that make up the organisms in an ecosystem are cycled repeatedly between the living and nonliving parts of the ecosystem. Food webs model how matter and energy are transferred among producers, consumers, and decomposers as the three groups interact within an ecosystem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a food web model to trace both matter and energy and explain how atoms are reused.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that atoms cycle between living and nonliving parts of ecosystems and food webs show how matter and energy are transferred.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw a food web with producers, consumers, and decomposers, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a producer and a consumer.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.B: Cycles of Matter and Energy Transfer in Ecosystems
text: Photosynthesis and cellular respiration provide most of the energy for life processes. Only a fraction of matter consumed at the lower level of a food web is transferred up, resulting in fewer organisms at higher levels. At each link in an ecosystem, elements are combined in different ways, and matter and energy are conserved. Photosynthesis and cellular respiration are key components of the global carbon cycle.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can calculate energy transfer between trophic levels and explain why there are fewer top predators.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that photosynthesis and respiration power life and only part of the matter and energy moves up a food web.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use an energy pyramid to show energy decreasing at each level, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the levels of a food chain.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.C: Ecosystem Dynamics, Functioning, and Resilience
text: When the environment changes, some organisms survive and reproduce, some move to new locations, some move into transformed environments, and some die.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict and explain what different organisms will do when their environment changes, using evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that when the environment changes, some organisms survive and reproduce, some move, and some die.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what happened to one organism when its environment changed, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that animals can be harmed when their home changes.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.C: Ecosystem Dynamics, Functioning, and Resilience
text: Ecosystem characteristics vary over time. Disruptions to any part of an ecosystem can lead to shifts in all of its populations. The completeness or integrity of an ecosystem’s biodiversity is often used as a measure of its health.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use biodiversity data to judge the health of an ecosystem and predict effects of a disruption.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that ecosystems change over time, disruptions shift populations, and biodiversity measures ecosystem health.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one disruption changed an ecosystem, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name things that disrupt ecosystems, such as pollution.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.C: Ecosystem Dynamics, Functioning, and Resilience
text: If a biological or physical disturbance to an ecosystem occurs, including one induced by human activity, the ecosystem may return to its more or less original state or become a very different ecosystem, depending on the complex set of interactions within the ecosystem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence from a real disturbance to predict whether the ecosystem will recover or change.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that after a disturbance an ecosystem may return to its original state or become a very different ecosystem.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how an ecosystem changed after a disturbance, using a case study with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name events that disturb ecosystems.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.D: Social Interactions and Group Behavior
text: Being part of a group helps animals obtain food, defend themselves, and cope with changes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare group behaviors of different animals and explain how each helps survival.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that living in a group helps animals get food, defend themselves, and cope with change.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one example of animals in a group helping each other, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name animals that live in groups.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.D: Social Interactions and Group Behavior
text: Changes in biodiversity can influence humans’ resources, such as food, energy, and medicines, as well as ecosystem services that humans rely on, for example, water purification and recycling.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a loss of biodiversity would affect a specific human resource and ecosystem service.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that changes in biodiversity affect human resources such as food and medicine and ecosystem services such as clean water.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name a resource people get from nature and how it could be lost, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people get food and water from nature.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.D: Social Interactions and Group Behavior
text: Changes in biodiversity can influence humans’ resources, such as food, energy, and medicines, as well as ecosystem services that humans rely on, for example, water purification and recycling.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a loss of biodiversity would affect a specific human resource and ecosystem service.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that changes in biodiversity affect human resources such as food and medicine and ecosystem services such as clean water.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name a resource people get from nature and how it could be lost, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people get food and water from nature.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.D: Social Interactions and Group Behavior
text: Changes in biodiversity can influence humans’ resources, such as food, energy, and medicines, as well as ecosystem services that humans rely on, for example, water purification and recycling.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a loss of biodiversity would affect a specific human resource and ecosystem service.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that changes in biodiversity affect human resources such as food and medicine and ecosystem services such as clean water.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name a resource people get from nature and how it could be lost, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people get food and water from nature.

subject: Science
cluster: LS2.D: Social Interactions and Group Behavior
text: Group behavior has evolved because membership can increase the chances of survival for individuals and their genetic relatives.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence for how group behavior increases survival of individuals and their relatives.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that group behavior evolved because it increases survival chances for individuals and their genetic relatives.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe an example of group behavior and its benefit, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name animals that live in groups.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3.A: Inheritance of Traits
text: Young organisms are very much, but not exactly, like their parents, and also resemble other organisms of the same kind.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how young organisms are like and unlike their parents and other organisms of the same kind.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that young organisms are like, but not exactly like, their parents and resemble others of the same kind.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one way a young animal looks like its parent, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match young animals to their parents.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3.A: Inheritance of Traits
text: Many characteristics of organisms are inherited from their parents. Other characteristics result from individuals’ interactions with the environment. Many characteristics involve both inheritance and environment.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can sort traits into inherited, environmental, or both and justify each choice with evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that many traits are inherited, others come from the environment, and many involve both.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one inherited trait and one trait caused by the environment, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that children look like their parents.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3.A: Inheritance of Traits
text: Genes chiefly regulate a specific protein, which affect an individual’s traits.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a gene's protein leads to a specific trait, using an example.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that genes mainly control specific proteins, which affect an individual's traits.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can say that genes carry information for traits, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some traits, such as eye color.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3.A: Inheritance of Traits
text: Genes chiefly regulate a specific protein, which affect an individual’s traits.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a gene's protein leads to a specific trait, using an example.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that genes mainly control specific proteins, which affect an individual's traits.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can say that genes carry information for traits, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some traits, such as eye color.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3.A: Inheritance of Traits
text: DNA carries instructions for forming species’ characteristics. Each cell in an organism has the same genetic content, but genes expressed by cells can differ.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why cells with the same DNA can be different, using gene expression in specific cell types.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that DNA carries instructions for traits and that all cells have the same DNA but express different genes.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe that DNA is in every cell and carries instructions, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that DNA is found in cells.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3.B: Variation of Traits
text: Individuals of the same kind of plant or animal are recognizable as similar, but can also vary in many ways.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare variation among individuals of the same kind and explain why they still belong together.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that individuals of the same kind of plant or animal are similar but vary in many ways.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one way two animals of the same kind are different, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to differences between two animals of the same kind.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3.B: Variation of Traits
text: Different organisms vary in how they look and function because they have different inherited information; the environment also affects the traits that an organism develops.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use evidence to explain how both inherited information and environment shape an organism's traits.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that organisms vary because of different inherited information and that the environment also affects traits.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how a plant's environment changed its growth, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that living things of the same kind can look different.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3.B: Variation of Traits
text: In sexual reproduction, each parent contributes half of the genes acquired by the offspring resulting in variation between parent and offspring. Genetic information can be altered because of mutations, which may result in beneficial, negative, or no change to proteins in or traits of an organism.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict variation in offspring and explain how a mutation could be beneficial, harmful, or neutral.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that each parent gives half the genes in sexual reproduction, causing variation, and that mutations can change genetic information.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain that offspring get genes from both parents, using a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that babies get traits from both parents.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3.B: Variation of Traits
text: In sexual reproduction, each parent contributes half of the genes acquired by the offspring resulting in variation between parent and offspring. Genetic information can be altered because of mutations, which may result in beneficial, negative, or no change to proteins in or traits of an organism.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict variation in offspring and explain how a mutation could be beneficial, harmful, or neutral.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that each parent gives half the genes in sexual reproduction, causing variation, and that mutations can change genetic information.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain that offspring get genes from both parents, using a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that babies get traits from both parents.

subject: Science
cluster: LS3.B: Variation of Traits
text: The variation and distribution of traits in a population depend on genetic and environmental factors. Genetic variation can result from mutations caused by environmental factors or errors in DNA replication, or from chromosomes swapping sections during meiosis.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how meiosis, replication errors, and environmental mutations each create variation, with examples.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that trait variation depends on genetic and environmental factors and that genetic variation comes from mutations and meiosis.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one source of genetic variation, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people in a population have different traits.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.A: Evidence of Common Ancestry and Diversity
text: Some living organisms resemble organisms that once lived on Earth. Fossils provide evidence about the types of organisms and environments that existed long ago.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use fossil evidence to describe past organisms and environments and compare them to today.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that fossils give evidence about organisms and environments from long ago and that some living things resemble them.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can match a fossil to a living organism it looks like, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that fossils are remains of old living things.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.A: Evidence of Common Ancestry and Diversity
text: The fossil record documents the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of many life forms and their environments through Earth’s history. The fossil record and comparisons of anatomical similarities between organisms enables the inference of lines of evolutionary descent.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use fossil and anatomical evidence to infer relationships between organisms and describe changes over time.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that the fossil record and anatomical similarities document change in life forms and allow inference of evolutionary lines.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a pattern in the fossil record, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that fossils show life from long ago.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.A: Evidence of Common Ancestry and Diversity
text: The ongoing branching that produces multiple lines of descent can be inferred by comparing DNA sequences, amino acid sequences, and anatomical and embryological evidence of different organisms.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare DNA, protein, and anatomical evidence to build and defend a branching tree of relationships.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that lines of descent can be inferred by comparing DNA, amino acid sequences, and anatomical and embryo evidence.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a simple evolutionary tree and identify close relatives, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that similar organisms may be related.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.B: Natural Selection
text: Differences in characteristics between individuals of the same species provide advantages in surviving and reproducing.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how a specific difference gives some individuals an advantage in a given environment.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that differences between individuals of the same species can give advantages in surviving and reproducing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a trait that helps an animal survive, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice differences between animals of the same kind.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.B: Natural Selection
text: Both natural and artificial selection result from certain traits giving some individuals an advantage in surviving and reproducing, leading to predominance of certain traits in a population.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare natural and artificial selection using examples and explain how each changes a population.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that natural and artificial selection happen when some traits give an advantage, making those traits more common.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give an example of natural or artificial selection, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that farmers choose the best plants or animals to breed.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.B: Natural Selection
text: Natural selection occurs only if there is variation in the genes and traits between organisms in a population. Traits that positively affect survival can become more common in a population.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use data to show how variation and selection pressure change trait frequency over generations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that natural selection needs genetic variation and that traits helping survival become more common.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how a helpful trait spreads in a population, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that animals with helpful traits survive better.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.C: Adaptation
text: Particular organisms can only survive in particular environments.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why a specific organism survives in one environment but not another, using its traits.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that particular organisms can only survive in particular environments.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can match an organism to the environment where it lives, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say where some animals live, such as fish in water.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Science 2017 (dpi.wi.gov); printed in source as SCI.LS4.A.3

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.C: Adaptation
text: Species can change over time in response to changes in environmental conditions through adaptation by natural selection acting over generations. Traits that support successful survival and reproduction in the new environment become more common.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how a species adapted over generations to a changed environment.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that species change over time as natural selection makes traits suited to a new environment more common.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe an adaptation and how it helps in an environment, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name an adaptation of an animal.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.C: Adaptation
text: Evolution results primarily from genetic variation of individuals in a species, competition for resources, and proliferation of organisms better able to survive and reproduce. Adaptation means that the distribution of traits in a population, as well as species expansion, emergence, or extinction, can change when conditions change.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use the factors of evolution to explain adaptation, speciation, or extinction in a real example.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that evolution results from genetic variation, competition, and better survival and reproduction, causing adaptation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name the main factors of evolution and give an example, with a graphic organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that species can change over a long time.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.D: Biodiversity and Humans
text: There are many different kinds of living things in any area, and they exist in different places on land and in water.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare the variety of living things in two habitats and explain why they differ.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that there are many kinds of living things in any area, living in different places on land and in water.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name living things found on land and in water, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort animals into land and water animals.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Science 2017 (dpi.wi.gov); printed in source as SCI.LS1.D.2

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.D: Biodiversity and Humans
text: Populations of organisms live in a variety of habitats. Change in those habitats affects the organisms living there.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict how a habitat change would affect several populations and explain why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that populations live in many habitats and that habitat change affects the organisms living there.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one habitat change affected an animal, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name different habitats, such as desert and ocean.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.D: Biodiversity and Humans
text: Changes in biodiversity can influence humans’ resources and ecosystem services they rely on.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a biodiversity change in a specific ecosystem affects human resources and services.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that changes in biodiversity influence human resources and the ecosystem services people rely on.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one ecosystem service, such as clean water, and how it depends on biodiversity, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people depend on plants and animals.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.D: Biodiversity and Humans
text: Changes in biodiversity can influence humans’ resources and ecosystem services they rely on.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a biodiversity change in a specific ecosystem affects human resources and services.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that changes in biodiversity influence human resources and the ecosystem services people rely on.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one ecosystem service, such as clean water, and how it depends on biodiversity, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people depend on plants and animals.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.D: Biodiversity and Humans
text: Changes in biodiversity can influence humans’ resources and ecosystem services they rely on.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a biodiversity change in a specific ecosystem affects human resources and services.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that changes in biodiversity influence human resources and the ecosystem services people rely on.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one ecosystem service, such as clean water, and how it depends on biodiversity, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people depend on plants and animals.

subject: Science
cluster: LS4.D: Biodiversity and Humans
text: Biodiversity is increased by formation of new species and reduced by extinction. Humans depend on biodiversity but also have adverse impacts on it. Sustaining biodiversity is essential to supporting life on Earth.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how human actions increase or reduce biodiversity and propose ways to sustain it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that biodiversity increases with new species and decreases with extinction and that humans depend on and affect it.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one way humans harm biodiversity and one way they protect it, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what biodiversity means, with a picture.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.A: Structure and Function
text: Matter exists as different substances that have different observable properties. Different properties are suited to different purposes. Objects can be built up from smaller parts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose the best material for a purpose by testing its properties and explain my choice.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that substances have different observable properties suited to different purposes and that objects can be built from smaller parts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a material as hard, soft, rough, or smooth, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort objects by what they are made of, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.A: Structure and Function
text: Matter exists as particles that are too small to see. Matter is always conserved even if it seems to disappear. Measurements of a variety of observable properties can be used to identify particular materials.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use measurements of several properties to identify an unknown material and explain conservation of matter.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that matter is made of particles too small to see, is always conserved, and can be identified by measuring properties.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can measure a property such as mass or magnetism to help identify a material, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that sugar seems to disappear in water but is still there.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.A: Structure and Function
text: The fact that matter is composed of atoms and molecules can be used to explain the properties of substances, diversity of materials, states of matter, phase changes, and conservation of matter.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use an atomic model to explain a property, phase change, and conservation of matter in one example.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the idea that matter is made of atoms and molecules to explain properties, states of matter, phase changes, and conservation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe particles in solids, liquids, and gases, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that matter is made of tiny particles.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.A: Structure and Function
text: The fact that matter is composed of atoms and molecules can be used to explain the properties of substances, diversity of materials, states of matter, phase changes, and conservation of matter.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use an atomic model to explain a property, phase change, and conservation of matter in one example.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the idea that matter is made of atoms and molecules to explain properties, states of matter, phase changes, and conservation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe particles in solids, liquids, and gases, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that matter is made of tiny particles.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.A: Structure and Function
text: The fact that matter is composed of atoms and molecules can be used to explain the properties of substances, diversity of materials, states of matter, phase changes, and conservation of matter.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use an atomic model to explain a property, phase change, and conservation of matter in one example.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the idea that matter is made of atoms and molecules to explain properties, states of matter, phase changes, and conservation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe particles in solids, liquids, and gases, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that matter is made of tiny particles.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.A: Structure and Function
text: The sub-atomic structural model and interactions between electric charges at the atomic scale can be used to explain the structure and interactions of matter, including chemical reactions and nuclear processes. Repeating patterns of the periodic table reflect patterns of outer electrons. A stable molecule has less energy than the same set of atoms separated; one must provide at least this energy to take the molecule apart.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use atomic structure and periodic patterns to predict and explain the behavior of matter in a new reaction.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the sub-atomic model and electric charge interactions to explain matter's structure, reactions, and periodic table patterns.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe protons, neutrons, and electrons and find valence electrons, with a periodic table.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the parts of an atom, using a model.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.B: Chemical Reactions
text: Heating or cooling a substance may cause changes that can be observed. Sometimes these changes are reversible, and sometimes they are not.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict whether a change from heating or cooling can be reversed and test my prediction.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that heating or cooling can cause observable changes and that some changes can be reversed and some cannot.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort changes, such as melting ice and cooking an egg, into reversible and not reversible, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that ice melts when it gets warm.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.B: Chemical Reactions
text: Chemical reactions that occur when substances are mixed can be identified by the emergence of substances with different properties. In chemical reactions the total mass remains the same. Note: At this level, students are not expected to differentiate between mass and weight.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design an investigation to show a new substance forms and that total mass stays the same.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that mixing substances can make new substances with different properties and that total mass stays the same.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe signs that a new substance formed after mixing, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can observe changes when two substances are mixed.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.B: Chemical Reactions
text: Reacting substances rearrange to form different molecules, but the number of atoms is conserved. Some reactions release energy and others absorb energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to show atoms rearranging in a reaction and explain why it releases or absorbs energy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that reacting substances rearrange into new molecules, atoms are conserved, and reactions release or absorb energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can count atoms before and after a reaction model, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that chemical reactions make new substances.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.B: Chemical Reactions
text: Reacting substances rearrange to form different molecules, but the number of atoms is conserved. Some reactions release energy and others absorb energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a model to show atoms rearranging in a reaction and explain why it releases or absorbs energy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that reacting substances rearrange into new molecules, atoms are conserved, and reactions release or absorb energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can count atoms before and after a reaction model, with support.
