descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that chemical reactions make new substances.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.B: Chemical Reactions
text: Chemical processes are understood in terms of collisions of molecules, rearrangement of atoms, and changes in energy as determined by properties of elements involved.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict reaction outcomes and rates using collision theory, atomic rearrangement, and energy changes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain chemical processes in terms of molecular collisions, rearrangement of atoms, and energy changes.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how collisions between particles lead to reactions, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify reactants and products in an equation.

subject: Science
cluster: PS1.C: Nuclear Processes
text: Nuclear processes, including fusion, fission, and radioactive decays of unstable nuclei, involve release or absorption of energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare fusion, fission, and decay and calculate or explain the energy involved in each.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that nuclear processes such as fusion, fission, and radioactive decay release or absorb energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the difference between fission and fusion, using diagrams.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that the nucleus is in the center of an atom.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2.A: Forces and Motion
text: Pushes and pulls can have different strengths and directions, and can change the speed or direction of an object’s motion, or start or stop it. A bigger push or pull makes things speed up or slow down more quickly.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict how a stronger or weaker push will change an object's motion and test it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that pushes and pulls have different strengths and directions and can start, stop, or change an object's motion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can show a push and a pull and say what happened to the object, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can push or pull a toy to make it move.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2.A: Forces and Motion
text: Qualities of motion and changes in motion require description of both size and direction. The effect of unbalanced forces on an object results in a change of motion. Patterns of motion can be used to predict future motion.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use patterns of motion to predict future motion and explain the effect of unbalanced forces.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe motion by size and direction, explain that unbalanced forces change motion, and use patterns to predict motion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify balanced and unbalanced forces in a picture, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say which way an object moves when pushed.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2.A: Forces and Motion
text: Motion and changes in motion can be qualitatively described using concepts of speed, velocity, and acceleration (including speeding up, slowing down, and/or changing direction). The role of the mass of an object must be qualitatively accounted for in any change of motion due to the application of a force (Newton’s first and second law). For any pair of interacting objects, the force exerted by the first object on the second object is equal in strength to the force that the second object exerts on the first, but in the opposite direction (Newton’s third law).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how force and mass together change an object's speed, velocity, or acceleration, with examples.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe motion using speed, velocity, and acceleration and account for the role of mass in changes of motion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can calculate speed from distance and time, with a worked example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say whether an object is speeding up or slowing down.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2.A: Forces and Motion
text: Motion and changes in motion can be quantitatively described using concepts of speed, velocity, and acceleration (including speeding up, slowing down, and/or changing direction). Newton’s second law of motion (F=ma) and the conservation of momentum can be used to predict changes in the motion of macroscopic objects. If a system interacts with objects outside itself, the total momentum of the system can change; however, any such change is balanced by changes in the momentum of objects outside the system.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use F = ma and momentum to analyze and predict motion in a complex situation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe motion quantitatively and use Newton's second law and conservation of momentum to predict changes.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use F = ma or p = mv to solve a simple problem, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can define speed, velocity, and acceleration, with a word bank.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2.B: Types of Interactions
text: When objects touch or collide, they push on one another and can result in a change of motion.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict and explain what will happen when two objects collide.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that when objects touch or collide they push on each other and can change motion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can show what happens when one ball hits another, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can roll a ball to hit another object.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2.B: Types of Interactions
text: Some forces act through contact, some forces (e.g. magnetic, electrostatic) act even when the objects are not in contact.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design a test to compare contact and non-contact forces and explain the results.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that some forces act through contact and some, like magnetic and electric forces, act without touching.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can show a magnet moving an object without touching it, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that magnets pull some objects.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2.B: Types of Interactions
text: The gravitational force of Earth acting on an object near Earth’s surface pulls that object toward the planet’s center.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why objects fall toward Earth's center everywhere on the planet, using a diagram.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that Earth's gravity pulls objects near its surface toward the planet's center.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can show that dropped objects fall down, with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that things fall to the ground.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2.B: Types of Interactions
text: Forces that act at a distance involve fields that can be mapped by their relative strength and effect on an object.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can map a field and explain how its strength changes with distance.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that forces acting at a distance involve fields that can be mapped by their strength and effect.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use iron filings or a compass to show a magnetic field, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that magnets can push or pull without touching.

subject: Science
cluster: PS2.B: Types of Interactions
text: Forces at a distance are explained by fields that can transfer energy and can be described in terms of the arrangement and properties of the interacting objects and the distance between them. These forces can be used to describe the relationship between electrical and magnetic fields. Attraction and repulsion between electric charges at the atomic scale explain the structure, properties, and transformations of matter, as well as the contact forces between material objects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use field models to explain and predict how electric and magnetic forces and energy change with distance.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that forces at a distance are described by fields that transfer energy and depend on the objects and distance.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how distance affects gravitational or electric force, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name forces that act at a distance.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.A: Definitions of Energy
text: Moving objects contain energy. The faster the object moves, the more energy it has.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design a test to show that faster objects have more energy and explain my evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that moving objects have energy and faster objects have more energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare two moving objects and say which has more energy, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that moving things have energy.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.A: Definitions of Energy
text: Kinetic energy can be distinguished from the various forms of potential energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can identify kinetic and several forms of potential energy in a system and explain how they change.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can distinguish kinetic energy from the different forms of potential energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort examples into kinetic or potential energy, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name kinetic and potential energy.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.A: Definitions of Energy
text: Kinetic energy can be distinguished from the various forms of potential energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can identify kinetic and several forms of potential energy in a system and explain how they change.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can distinguish kinetic energy from the different forms of potential energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort examples into kinetic or potential energy, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name kinetic and potential energy.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.A: Definitions of Energy
text: Systems move towards more stable states.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with examples why systems move toward more stable, lower energy states.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that systems move toward more stable states.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give an example of a system becoming more stable, such as a ball rolling downhill, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that a ball rolls down and stops.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.B: Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer
text: Energy can be moved from place to place by moving objects, or through sound, light, or electrical currents. Energy can be converted from one form to another form.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build a device that converts energy and explain each transfer and conversion.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that energy moves by moving objects, sound, light, or electric currents and can change from one form to another.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name ways energy moves, such as light and sound, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that a lamp gives light.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.B: Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer
text: Energy changes to and from each type can be tracked through physical or chemical interactions. The relationship between the temperature and the total energy of a system depends on the types, states, and amounts of matter.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can track energy changes in a process and explain how temperature relates to total energy for different materials.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can track energy changes in physical and chemical interactions and explain how temperature and total energy depend on matter.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe an energy transfer in a simple system, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that heat moves from hot to cold.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.B: Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer
text: The total energy within a system is conserved. Energy transfer within and between systems can be described and predicted in terms of energy associated with the motion or configuration of particles (objects).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can calculate energy in a system and predict transfers using motion and configuration energy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that energy is conserved in a system and describe transfers using energy of motion and position of particles.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can complete an energy bar chart for a simple system, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that energy is not created or destroyed.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.B: Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer
text: The total energy within a system is conserved. Energy transfer within and between systems can be described and predicted in terms of energy associated with the motion or configuration of particles (objects).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can calculate energy in a system and predict transfers using motion and configuration energy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that energy is conserved in a system and describe transfers using energy of motion and position of particles.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can complete an energy bar chart for a simple system, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that energy is not created or destroyed.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.C: Relationships between Energy and Forces
text: Bigger pushes and pulls cause bigger changes in an object’s motion or shape.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can test and explain how changing push strength changes motion or shape.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that bigger pushes and pulls cause bigger changes in motion or shape.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare a big and small push and what happened, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can push a toy hard and soft.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.C: Relationships between Energy and Forces
text: When objects collide, contact forces transfer energy so as to change objects’ motions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict and explain energy transfer in collisions of different speeds.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that in collisions, contact forces transfer energy and change objects' motions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what happens to two objects after they collide, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can observe two objects bumping into each other.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.C: Relationships between Energy and Forces
text: When two objects interact, each one exerts a force on the other, and these forces can transfer energy between the interacting objects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how forces transfer energy in a real interaction and predict the outcome.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that interacting objects exert forces on each other that can transfer energy between them.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the forces and energy change when two objects interact, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that objects push on each other when they touch.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.C: Relationships between Energy and Forces
text: Fields contain energy that depends on the arrangement of the objects in the field.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how changing the arrangement of objects in a field changes the stored energy, with calculations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that fields contain energy that depends on the arrangement of objects in the field.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how moving magnets closer changes stored energy, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name gravitational, electric, and magnetic fields.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.D: Energy in Chemical Processes and Everyday Life
text: Sunlight warms Earth’s surface.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare how sunlight warms different surfaces and explain my results.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that sunlight warms Earth's surface.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can feel and compare a surface in sun and shade, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun makes things warm.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.D: Energy in Chemical Processes and Everyday Life
text: Plants capture energy from sunlight which can be used as fuel or food. Stored energy in food or fuel can be converted to useable energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can trace energy from the sun into plants and food or fuel and explain how it is released.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants capture energy from sunlight for food or fuel and that stored energy can be converted to useful energy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe that food energy comes from plants and the sun, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants need sunlight.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.D: Energy in Chemical Processes and Everyday Life
text: Sunlight is captured by plants and used in a chemical reaction to produce sugar molecules for storing this energy. This stored energy can be released by respiration or combustion, which can be reversed by burning those molecules to release energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how energy stored in sugar by photosynthesis is released by respiration or combustion.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants store sunlight energy in sugars and that this energy is released by respiration or combustion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the energy changes in photosynthesis, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants store energy from the sun.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.D: Energy in Chemical Processes and Everyday Life
text: Sunlight is captured by plants and used in a chemical reaction to produce sugar molecules for storing this energy. This stored energy can be released by respiration or combustion, which can be reversed by burning those molecules to release energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how energy stored in sugar by photosynthesis is released by respiration or combustion.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants store sunlight energy in sugars and that this energy is released by respiration or combustion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the energy changes in photosynthesis, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants store energy from the sun.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.D: Energy in Chemical Processes and Everyday Life
text: Sunlight is captured by plants and used in a chemical reaction to produce sugar molecules for storing this energy. This stored energy can be released by respiration or combustion, which can be reversed by burning those molecules to release energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how energy stored in sugar by photosynthesis is released by respiration or combustion.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants store sunlight energy in sugars and that this energy is released by respiration or combustion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the energy changes in photosynthesis, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants store energy from the sun.

subject: Science
cluster: PS3.D: Energy in Chemical Processes and Everyday Life
text: Photosynthesis is the primary biological means of capturing radiation from the sun; energy cannot be destroyed, but it can be converted to less useful forms.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how photosynthesis captures solar energy and why energy becomes less useful in each transfer.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that photosynthesis captures the sun's radiation and that energy is converted to less useful forms but not destroyed.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how energy changes form in photosynthesis, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that plants capture the sun's energy.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.A: Wave Properties
text: Sound can make matter vibrate, and vibrating matter can make sound.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can show that sound makes things vibrate and vibrations make sound, and explain my evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that sound can make matter vibrate and vibrating matter can make sound.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can feel a vibration when I make a sound, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can make sounds with objects.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.A: Wave Properties
text: Waves are regular patterns of motion, which can be made in water by disturbing the surface. Waves of the same type can differ in amplitude and wavelength. Waves can make objects move.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can make waves with different amplitudes and wavelengths and explain how waves can move objects.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that waves are regular patterns of motion that differ in amplitude and wavelength and can move objects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label the amplitude and wavelength of a wave, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can make a wave in water.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.A: Wave Properties
text: A simple wave model has a repeating pattern with a specific wavelength, frequency, and amplitude, and mechanical waves need a medium through which they are transmitted. This model can explain many phenomena including sound and light. Waves can transmit energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a wave model to explain sound and light phenomena and how waves transmit energy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe a wave model with wavelength, frequency, and amplitude and explain that mechanical waves need a medium.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label parts of a wave and say that sound needs a medium, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can draw a wave.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Science 2017 (dpi.wi.gov); printed in source as SCI.PS4.C.m

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.A: Wave Properties
text: The wavelength and frequency of a wave are related to one another by the speed of the wave, which depends on the type of wave and the medium through which it is passing. Waves can be used to transmit information and energy.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can calculate wave properties in different media and explain how waves carry information and energy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that wavelength and frequency are related by wave speed, which depends on the wave and medium.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use v = f x wavelength with given values, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can define wavelength and frequency.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.B: Electro-magnetic Radiation
text: Objects can be seen only when light is available to illuminate them.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can test which objects can be seen in different light conditions and explain the results.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that objects can be seen only when there is light to illuminate them.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can show that I cannot see in a dark box until light shines in, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that we need light to see.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.B: Electro-magnetic Radiation
text: Objects can be seen when light reflected from their surface enters our eyes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can model how light reflects from objects into the eye and explain how mirrors work.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that we see objects when light reflected from them enters our eyes.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw arrows to show light going from an object to my eye, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that eyes need light to see.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.B: Electro-magnetic Radiation
text: The construct of a wave is used to model how light interacts with objects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a wave model to predict how light will reflect, refract, or be absorbed by different objects.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use a wave model to explain how light interacts with objects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe reflection and absorption of light, with a diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that light can bounce off objects.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.B: Electro-magnetic Radiation
text: Both an electromagnetic wave model and a photon model explain features of electromagnetic radiation broadly and describe common applications of electromagnetic radiation.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain when a wave model or photon model better explains electromagnetic radiation and its uses.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that wave and photon models both explain features and applications of electromagnetic radiation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name types of electromagnetic radiation and a use for each, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that light is a type of electromagnetic radiation.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.C: Information Technologies and Instru-mentation
text: People use devices to send and receive information.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design a device to send a message over a distance and explain how it works.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that people use devices to send and receive information.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name devices that send messages, such as phones, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can show how I can send a message by waving or calling.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.C: Information Technologies and Instru-mentation
text: Patterns can encode, send, receive, and decode information.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create my own code to send and decode a message and compare it with others.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that patterns can encode, send, receive, and decode information.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a given code, such as Morse code, to send a message, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can follow a simple pattern of sounds or lights.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.C: Information Technologies and Instru-mentation
text: Waves can be used to transmit digital information. Digitized information is comprised of a pattern of 1s and 0s.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a digital signal of 1s and 0s is sent by waves and why it is reliable.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that waves can transmit digital information made of patterns of 1s and 0s.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can show how a message can be written as 1s and 0s, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name devices that use digital information.

subject: Science
cluster: PS4.C: Information Technologies and Instru-mentation
text: Large amounts of information can be stored and shipped around as a result of being digitized.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how digitization allows large amounts of information to be stored and shared, including its risks.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that large amounts of information can be stored and shipped because it is digitized.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one advantage of digital storage, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name ways we store digital information.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.A: The Universe and Its Stars
text: Patterns of movement of the sun, moon, and stars, as seen from Earth, can be observed, described, and predicted.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict where the sun or moon will be at a later time using patterns I observed.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can observe, describe, and predict patterns of movement of the sun, moon, and stars as seen from Earth.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe where the sun is in the morning and afternoon, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to the sun and moon in pictures of day and night sky.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.A: The Universe and Its Stars
text: Stars range greatly in size and distance from Earth, and this can explain their relative brightness.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use data on size and distance to explain why the sun looks brighter than other stars.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that stars vary greatly in size and distance from Earth, which explains their relative brightness.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can say that the sun looks bright because it is close, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun is a star.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.A: The Universe and Its Stars
text: The solar system is part of the Milky Way, which is one of many billions of galaxies.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a scale model to explain our place in the Milky Way and the universe.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that the solar system is part of the Milky Way, one of billions of galaxies.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can order solar system, galaxy, and universe by size, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth is part of the solar system.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.A: The Universe and Its Stars
text: The solar system is part of the Milky Way, which is one of many billions of galaxies.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a scale model to explain our place in the Milky Way and the universe.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that the solar system is part of the Milky Way, one of billions of galaxies.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can order solar system, galaxy, and universe by size, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth is part of the solar system.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.A: The Universe and Its Stars
text: Light spectra from stars are used to determine their characteristics, processes, and lifecycles. Solar activity creates the elements through nuclear fusion. The development of technologies has provided the astronomical data that provide the empirical evidence for the Big Bang theory.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use light spectra data to infer a star's properties and explain how stars make elements.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that light spectra reveal star characteristics, stars make elements by fusion, and astronomical data supports theories of the universe.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how scientists use light from stars to learn about them, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that stars produce light.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.B: Earth and the Solar System
text: Seasonal patterns of sunrise and sunset can be observed, described, and predicted.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use observations to predict how daylight hours change through the year.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can observe, describe, and predict seasonal patterns of sunrise and sunset.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare when the sun rises in two seasons, using a chart with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that it is light in the day and dark at night.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.B: Earth and the Solar System
text: The Earth’s orbit and rotation, and the orbit of the moon around the Earth cause observable patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain several patterns, such as shadows, day length, and moon phases, using Earth's and the moon's motions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that Earth's orbit and rotation and the moon's orbit cause observable patterns.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can show with a model how Earth's spin causes day and night, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth spins and moves around the sun.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.B: Earth and the Solar System
text: The solar system contains many varied objects held together by gravity. Solar system models explain and predict eclipses, lunar phases, and seasons.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a solar system model to predict an eclipse or lunar phase and explain the role of gravity.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that gravity holds the solar system together and that models explain eclipses, lunar phases, and seasons.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a model to show the cause of one pattern, such as moon phases, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name objects in the solar system.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.B: Earth and the Solar System
text: The solar system contains many varied objects held together by gravity. Solar system models explain and predict eclipses, lunar phases, and seasons.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a solar system model to predict an eclipse or lunar phase and explain the role of gravity.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that gravity holds the solar system together and that models explain eclipses, lunar phases, and seasons.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a model to show the cause of one pattern, such as moon phases, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name objects in the solar system.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.B: Earth and the Solar System
text: Kepler’s laws describe common features of the motions of orbiting objects. Observations from astronomy and space probes provide evidence for explanations of solar system formation. Cyclical changes in Earth’s tilt and orbit, occurring over tens to hundreds of thousands of years, cause cycles of ice ages and other gradual climate changes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply Kepler's laws and orbital changes to explain solar system formation and long-term climate cycles.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that Kepler's laws describe orbits, space data supports solar system formation ideas, and orbital changes affect climate.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe an elliptical orbit and one of Kepler's laws, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that planets orbit the sun.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.C: The History of Planet Earth
text: Some events on Earth occur very quickly; others can occur very slowly.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare fast and slow Earth events and give evidence for how long each takes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that some events on Earth happen very quickly and others very slowly.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort events, such as earthquakes and erosion, into fast or slow, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that some changes to land happen fast.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.C: The History of Planet Earth
text: Certain features on Earth can be used to order events that have occurred in a landscape.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use rock layers and fossils to put a series of events in order and explain my reasoning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that certain features on Earth can be used to order events in a landscape.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can say which rock layer formed first, with a diagram and support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice layers in rocks.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.C: The History of Planet Earth
text: Rock strata and the fossil record can be used as evidence to organize the relative occurrence of major historical events in Earth’s history.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use rock strata and fossils to build a timeline of major events and justify the order.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that rock strata and the fossil record are evidence for the order of major events in Earth's history.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use rock layers to put events in order, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that lower layers are usually older.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1.C: The History of Planet Earth
text: The rock record resulting from tectonic and other geoscience processes as well as objects from the solar system can provide evidence of Earth’s early history and the relative ages of major geologic formations.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can combine rock record and meteorite evidence to explain Earth's early history and date formations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that the rock record and solar system objects give evidence of Earth's early history and the ages of formations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how scientists date rocks, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth is very old.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.A: Earth Materials and Systems
text: Wind and water change the shape of the land.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design a model to show how wind or water changes land and explain how to slow it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that wind and water change the shape of the land.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can show how water moves sand in a tray, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that wind blows sand.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.A: Earth Materials and Systems
text: Rainfall helps to shape the land and affects the types of living things found in a region. Water, ice, wind, organisms, and gravity break rocks, soils, and sediments into smaller pieces and move them around.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how weathering and erosion shaped a real landscape and its living things.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that rainfall shapes land and affects living things, and that water, ice, wind, organisms, and gravity break and move rock and soil.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how water or wind breaks down rock, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that rocks can break into small pieces.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.A: Earth Materials and Systems
text: Four major Earth systems (geosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere) interact.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can model how the four Earth systems interact in a real example, such as a sandstorm.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that the geosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, and hydrosphere interact.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name the four Earth systems and give one example of each, with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name land, water, air, and living things.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.A: Earth Materials and Systems
text: Energy flows and matter cycles within and among Earth’s systems, including the sun and Earth’s interior as primary energy sources. Plate tectonics is one result of these processes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how energy from the sun and Earth's interior drives matter cycles and plate tectonics.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that energy flows and matter cycles in Earth's systems, powered by the sun and Earth's interior, and that plate tectonics results.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one Earth cycle and its energy source, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the sun as a source of energy for Earth.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.A: Earth Materials and Systems
text: Energy flows and matter cycles within and among Earth’s systems, including the sun and Earth’s interior as primary energy sources. Plate tectonics is one result of these processes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how energy from the sun and Earth's interior drives matter cycles and plate tectonics.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that energy flows and matter cycles in Earth's systems, powered by the sun and Earth's interior, and that plate tectonics results.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one Earth cycle and its energy source, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the sun as a source of energy for Earth.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.A: Earth Materials and Systems
text: Feedback effects exist within and among Earth’s systems.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze data to show a chain of feedback effects among Earth's systems.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that feedback effects exist within and among Earth's systems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one feedback effect, such as melting ice, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name Earth's systems.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.B: Plate Tectonics and Large-Scale System Interactions
text: Maps show where things are located. One can map the shapes and kinds of land and water in any area.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can make a map of an area showing land and water features and explain what it shows.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that maps show where things are and can show the shapes and kinds of land and water in an area.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find land and water on a map, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to water and land in a picture.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.B: Plate Tectonics and Large-Scale System Interactions
text: Earth’s physical features occur in patterns, as do earthquakes and volcanoes. Maps can be used to locate features and determine patterns in those events.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze maps to explain patterns of mountains, earthquakes, and volcanoes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that Earth's features, earthquakes, and volcanoes occur in patterns that maps can show.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find where earthquakes happen on a map and describe a pattern, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name mountains, volcanoes, and oceans on a map.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.B: Plate Tectonics and Large-Scale System Interactions
text: Plate tectonics is the unifying theory that explains movements of rocks at Earth’s surface and geological history. Maps are used to display evidence of plate movement.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use map evidence to explain how plate movement formed specific features.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that plate tectonics explains rock movement and geologic history and that maps show evidence of plate movement.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify plate boundaries on a map, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth's crust is made of plates.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.B: Plate Tectonics and Large-Scale System Interactions
text: Radioactive decay within Earth’s interior contributes to thermal convection in the mantle.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how radioactive decay heats Earth's interior and drives mantle convection and plate motion.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that radioactive decay in Earth's interior contributes to thermal convection in the mantle.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw convection currents in the mantle, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name Earth's layers.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.C: The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface Processes
text: Water is found in many types of places and in different forms on Earth.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can map where water is found in my area and in what forms.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that water is found in many places and in different forms on Earth.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name places where water is found, such as the sea, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that water can be liquid or ice.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.C: The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface Processes
text: Most of Earth’s water is in the ocean, and much of the Earth’s freshwater is in glaciers or underground.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can graph Earth's water and explain why fresh water is precious in places like Qatar.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that most of Earth's water is in the ocean and much fresh water is in glaciers or underground.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a chart showing salt water and fresh water amounts, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that oceans have salt water.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.C: The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface Processes
text: Water cycles among land, ocean, and atmosphere, and is propelled by sunlight and gravity. Density variations of sea water drive interconnected ocean currents. Water movement causes weathering and erosion, changing landscape features.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how sunlight, gravity, and density differences move water and shape landscapes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that water cycles among land, ocean, and air, driven by sunlight and gravity, and causes weathering and erosion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label the water cycle and describe how water causes erosion, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that rain falls from clouds.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.C: The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface Processes
text: Water cycles among land, ocean, and atmosphere, and is propelled by sunlight and gravity. Density variations of sea water drive interconnected ocean currents. Water movement causes weathering and erosion, changing landscape features.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how sunlight, gravity, and density differences move water and shape landscapes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that water cycles among land, ocean, and air, driven by sunlight and gravity, and causes weathering and erosion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label the water cycle and describe how water causes erosion, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that rain falls from clouds.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.C: The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface Processes
text: The planet’s dynamics are greatly influenced by water’s unique chemical and physical properties.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can investigate a property of water and explain its effect on Earth's processes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that water's unique chemical and physical properties greatly influence Earth's dynamics.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name properties of water, such as expanding when it freezes, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that water can be solid, liquid, or gas.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.D: Weather and Climate
text: Weather is the combination of sunlight, wind, snow or rain, and temperature in a particular region and time. People record weather patterns over time.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can record weather over time and describe patterns I find.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe weather as sunlight, wind, rain, and temperature at a place and time and record it over time.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can record today's weather with symbols, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say if it is sunny or rainy.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.D: Weather and Climate
text: Climate describes patterns of typical weather conditions over different scales and variations. Historical weather patterns can be analyzed.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze weather data from two places and explain differences in their climates.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that climate describes patterns of typical weather and that past weather patterns can be analyzed.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a weather table for a season and describe the typical weather, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what the weather is usually like in summer.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.D: Weather and Climate
text: Complex interactions determine local weather patterns and influence climate, including the role of the ocean.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how ocean and air interactions create local weather and climate in a region.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that complex interactions, including the ocean, determine local weather and influence climate.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how the sea affects weather near the coast, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell the difference between weather and climate, with help.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.D: Weather and Climate
text: The role of radiation from the sun and its interactions with the atmosphere, ocean, and land are the foundation for the global climate system. Global climate models are used to predict future changes, including changes influenced by human behavior and natural factors.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use climate model results to explain how human and natural factors change global climate.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that solar radiation and its interactions form the climate system and that models predict future change.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the greenhouse effect using a diagram, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun warms Earth.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.E: Biogeology
text: Plants and animals can change their local environment.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can give several examples of how plants and animals change their environment and explain why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants and animals can change their local environment.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one example, such as a bird building a nest, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that animals dig holes or build homes.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.E: Biogeology
text: Living things can affect the physical characteristics of their environment.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how living things changed the physical features of a place.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that living things can affect the physical characteristics of their environment.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how plant roots can break rocks, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that animals change the places they live.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.E: Biogeology
text: The fossil record documents the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of many life forms throughout history (linked to content in LS4.A).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use fossil evidence to describe how life and environments changed over Earth's history.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that the fossil record documents the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life forms through history.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what fossils tell us about past life, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that fossils are evidence of past life.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.E: Biogeology
text: The fossil record documents the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of many life forms throughout history (linked to content in LS4.A).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use fossil evidence to describe how life and environments changed over Earth's history.

descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what fossils tell us about past life, with support.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2.E: Biogeology
text: The biosphere and Earth’s other systems have many interconnections that cause a continual coevolution of Earth’s surface and life on it.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can argue with evidence how life and Earth's surface have changed each other over time.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that the biosphere and Earth's other systems are interconnected and have coevolved over time.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one example of life changing Earth's systems, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that living things affect air, water, and land.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.A: Natural Resources
text: Living things need water, air, and resources from the land, and they live in places that have the things they need. Humans use natural resources for everything they do.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how different animals' homes give them what they need and how people use natural resources.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that living things need water, air, and land resources, live where they can get them, and that humans use natural resources.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can match an animal to the place it lives and what it needs, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that animals need water and food.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.A: Natural Resources
text: Energy and fuels humans use are derived from natural sources, and their use affects the environment. Some resources are renewable over time, others are not.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare renewable and nonrenewable energy sources and explain their effects on the environment.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that energy and fuels come from natural sources, their use affects the environment, and some are renewable.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort energy sources into renewable and nonrenewable, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name energy sources, such as the sun and oil.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.A: Natural Resources
text: Humans depend on Earth’s land, oceans, fresh water, atmosphere, and biosphere for different resources, many of which are limited or not renewable. Resources are distributed unevenly around the planet as a result of past geologic processes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence why resources are unevenly distributed and how this affects people.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that humans depend on limited Earth resources that are unevenly distributed because of past geologic processes.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe where a resource is found and why it is limited, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name natural resources.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.A: Natural Resources
text: Resource availability has guided the development of human society and use of natural resources has associated costs, risks, and benefits.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how a resource shaped a society, such as natural gas in Qatar, and weigh its costs and benefits.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that resource availability has guided human society and that using resources has costs, risks, and benefits.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can list a cost and a benefit of using a natural resource, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name resources people use.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.B: Natural Hazards
text: In a region, some kinds of severe weather are more likely than others. Forecasts allow communities to prepare for severe weather.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how forecasts help my community prepare for the severe weather common in our region.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that some severe weather is more likely in a region and that forecasts help communities prepare.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name a type of severe weather and one way to stay safe, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name types of weather, such as storms.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.B: Natural Hazards
text: A variety of hazards result from natural processes; humans cannot eliminate hazards but can reduce their impacts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare solutions that reduce the impact of a natural hazard and choose the best with reasons.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that natural processes cause hazards that humans cannot stop but can reduce their impacts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name a natural hazard and one way people reduce its harm, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name natural hazards, such as floods.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.B: Natural Hazards

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that natural processes cause hazards that humans cannot stop but can reduce their impacts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name a natural hazard and one way people reduce its harm, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name natural hazards, such as floods.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.B: Natural Hazards
text: Patterns can be seen through mapping the history of natural hazards in a region and understanding related geological forces.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze hazard maps and geologic data to forecast risk in a region.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that mapping the history of natural hazards and understanding geologic forces reveals patterns.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a pattern on a hazard map, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name places where earthquakes happen, using a map.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.B: Natural Hazards
text: Natural hazards and other geological events have shaped the course of human history at local, regional, and global scales.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how a natural hazard changed the history of a community or region.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that natural hazards and geologic events have shaped human history at local, regional, and global scales.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one natural hazard affected people, with a case study and support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name natural hazards.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.C: Human Impacts on Earth Systems
text: Things people do can affect the environment but they can make choices to reduce their impacts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can suggest several ways people can reduce their impact and explain how each helps.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that things people do affect the environment and that people can make choices to reduce their impact.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one way to help the environment, such as recycling, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that litter is bad for the environment.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.C: Human Impacts on Earth Systems
text: Societal activities have had major effects on the land, ocean, atmosphere, and even outer space. Societal activities can also help protect Earth’s resources and environments.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can research how a community protects resources and evaluate how well it works.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that human activities have affected land, ocean, air, and space and can also protect Earth's resources.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one human effect on the environment and one way to protect it, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name ways people protect nature.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.C: Human Impacts on Earth Systems
text: Human activities have altered the hydrosphere, atmosphere, and lithosphere which in turn has altered the biosphere. Changes to the biosphere can have different impacts for different living things. Activities and technologies can be engineered to reduce people’s impacts on Earth.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can trace how a human activity changes one sphere and then the biosphere, and propose a technology to reduce it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that human activities have altered Earth's spheres and biosphere and that technologies can be engineered to reduce impacts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how a human activity changes air, water, or land, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name ways people change the environment.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name ways people change the environment.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.C: Human Impacts on Earth Systems
text: Sustainability of human societies and the biodiversity that supports them requires responsible management of natural resources, including the development of technologies.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate a resource management plan and technology for sustaining people and biodiversity.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that sustaining societies and biodiversity requires responsible resource management, including new technologies.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one sustainable practice and why it matters, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what sustainability means, with an example.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.D: Global Climate Change
text: Evidence suggests human activities affect global warming. Decisions to reduce the impact of global warming depend on understanding climate science, engineering capabilities, and social dynamics.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence that human activities cause warming and propose solutions considering science, engineering, and society.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that evidence shows human activities affect global warming and that solutions depend on science, engineering, and social factors.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name a human activity that causes warming and one solution, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth is getting warmer.

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3.D: Global Climate Change
text: Global climate models used to predict changes continue to be improved, although discoveries about the global climate system are ongoing and continually needed.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the strengths and limits of climate models and explain how new evidence improves them.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that global climate models used to predict change keep improving as discoveries continue.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what a climate model predicts, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that scientists use models to predict climate.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1.A: Defining and Delimiting Engineering Problems
text: A situation that people want to change or create can be approached as a problem to be solved through engineering. Asking questions, making observations, and gathering information are helpful in thinking about problems. Before beginning to design a solution, it is important to clearly understand the problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask questions and gather information to clearly define a problem before designing.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that a situation people want to change can be a problem to solve and that asking questions and observing help define it.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a problem I want to solve, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say something that needs fixing.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1.A: Defining and Delimiting Engineering Problems
text: Possible solutions to a problem are limited by available materials and resources (constraints). The success of a designed solution is determined by considering the desired features of a solution (criteria). Different proposals for solutions can be compared on the basis of how well each one meets the specified criteria for success or how well each takes the constraints into account.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can define criteria and constraints and compare proposals using them.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that solutions are limited by constraints, judged by criteria, and can be compared on how well they meet both.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can list one criterion and one constraint for a design, with a template.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what my design needs to do.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1.A: Defining and Delimiting Engineering Problems
text: The more precisely a design task’s criteria and constraints can be defined, the more likely it is that the designed solution will be successful. Specification of constraints includes consideration of scientific principles and other relevant knowledge that are likely to limit possible solutions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can precisely define criteria and constraints, including scientific limits, for a design task.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that precisely defined criteria and constraints, including scientific principles, make a successful design more likely.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write criteria and constraints for a design task, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe a design problem.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1.A: Defining and Delimiting Engineering Problems
text: Criteria and constraints also include satisfying any requirements set by society, such as taking issues of risk mitigation into account, and they should be quantified to the extent possible and stated in such a way that one can tell if a given design meets them. Humanity faces major global challenges today, such as the need for supplies of clean water and food or for energy sources that minimize pollution, which can be addressed through engineering. These global challenges also may have manifestations in local communities.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can quantify criteria and constraints, including societal requirements and risk, for a global problem.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that criteria and constraints include societal requirements and should be quantified so designs can be checked.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write measurable criteria for a design, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can list what a solution must do.

cluster: ETS1.B: Developing Possible Solutions
text: Designs can be conveyed through sketches, drawings, or physical models. These representations are useful in communicating ideas for a problem’s solutions to other people.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can communicate my design idea clearly with a labeled sketch and a model.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that designs can be shared through sketches, drawings, or models.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw my design idea, with help.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1.B: Developing Possible Solutions
text: Research on a problem should be carried out before beginning to design a solution. Testing a solution involves investigating how well it performs under a range of likely conditions. At whatever stage, communicating with peers about proposed solutions is an important part of the design process, and shared ideas can lead to improved designs. Tests are often designed to identify failure points or difficulties, which suggest the elements of the design that need to be improved.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can research a problem, test my solution under different conditions, and use peer feedback to improve it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that research comes before designing, testing checks performance under different conditions, and sharing ideas helps.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can test my design and share results with a partner, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can test a design to see if it works.

cluster: ETS1.B: Developing Possible Solutions
text: A solution needs to be tested and then modified on the basis of the test results in order to improve it. cluster: ETS2.B: Influence of Engineering, Technology, and Science on Society and the Natural World
text: All human activity draws on natural resources and has both short-and long-term consequences, positive as well as negative, for the health of people and the natural environment. The uses of technologies are driven by people’s needs, desires, and values; by the findings of scientific research; and by differences in such factors as climate, natural resources, and economic conditions. Technology use varies over time and from region to region.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze the short and long-term effects of a technology on people and the environment.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that technologies use natural resources, have positive and negative effects, and are driven by people's needs and values.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can list one positive and one negative effect of a technology, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a technology and what it is used for.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS2.B: Influence of Engineering, Technology, and Science on Society and the Natural World
text: Modern civilization depends on major technological systems, such as agriculture, health, water, energy, transportation, manufacturing, construction, and communications. Engineers continuously modify these systems to increase benefits while decreasing costs and risks. New technologies can have deep impacts on society and the environment, including some that were not anticipated. Analysis of costs and benefits is a critical aspect of decisions about technology.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how engineers modify a major technological system, such as water or energy, to balance benefits and risks.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that society depends on major technological systems that engineers modify to increase benefits and reduce costs and risks.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a technological system, such as water supply, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name systems people depend on, such as electricity.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS3.A: Science and Engineering Are Human Endeavors
text: Individuals from diverse backgrounds bring unique perspectives that are valuable to the outcomes and processes of science and engineering. Scientists’ and engineers’ backgrounds, perspectives, and fields of endeavor influence the nature of questions they ask, the definition of problems, and the nature of their findings and solutions. Some cultures have historically been marginalized in science and engineering discourse. Scientists and engineers embrace skepticism and critique as a community. Deliberate deceit in science is rare and is likely exposed through the peer review process. When discovered, intellectual dishonesty is condemned by the scientific community.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how a scientist's background shaped their questions and how peer critique improved the work.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that diverse backgrounds bring valuable perspectives and influence the questions scientists and engineers ask.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how a scientist's background influenced their work, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that scientists come from many backgrounds.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS3.B: Science and Engineering Are Unique Ways of Thinking With Different Purposes
text: Science and engineering are both bodies of knowledge and processes that add new knowledge to our understanding. Scientific findings are limited to what can be supported with evidence from the natural world. Basic laws of nature are the same everywhere in the universe (e.g. gravity, conservation of matter, energy transfer, etc.). Engineering solutions often have drawbacks as well as benefits.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a scientific finding is supported by evidence and why laws of nature are the same everywhere.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that science and engineering are knowledge and processes, that findings need evidence, and that natural laws apply everywhere.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain why scientists need evidence, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that scientists collect evidence.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS3.B: Science and Engineering Are Unique Ways of Thinking With Different Purposes
text: Science asks questions to understand the natural world and assumes that objects and events in natural systems occur in consistent patterns that are understandable through measurement and observation. Science carefully considers and evaluates anomalies in data and evidence. Engineering seeks solutions to human problems, including issues that arise due to human interaction with the environment. It uses some of the same practices as science and often applies scientific principles to solutions. Science and engineering have direct impacts on the quality of life for all people. Therefore, scientists and engineers need to pursue their work in an ethical manner that requires honesty, fairness, and dedication to public health, safety, and welfare.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how scientists handle unexpected data and why some questions cannot be answered by science.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that science assumes consistent natural patterns, uses measurement and observation, and carefully evaluates anomalies in data.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what scientists do with surprising results, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that science asks questions about nature.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS3.B: Science and Engineering Are Unique Ways of Thinking With Different Purposes
text: Science is both a body of knowledge that represents current understanding of natural systems and the processes used to refine, elaborate, revise, and extend this knowledge. These processes differentiate science from other ways of knowing. Science knowledge has a history that includes the refinement of, and changes to, theories, ideas, and beliefs over time. Science and engineering innovations may raise ethical issues for which science and engineering, by themselves, do not provide answers and solutions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a scientific idea changed over history and what makes science different from other ways of knowing.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that science is both knowledge and processes for revising it and that these processes set science apart from other ways of knowing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one scientific idea changed over time, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that science knowledge can change with new evidence.

subject: Science

cluster: ETS3.C: Science and Engineering Use Multiple Approaches to Create New Knowledge and Solve Problems
text: Science and engineers use many approaches to answer questions about the natural world and solve problems. Scientific explanations are strengthened by being supported with evidence. An engineering problem can have many solutions. The strength of a solution depends on how well it solves the problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can give examples of different ways to answer a question and different solutions to one problem.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that scientists and engineers use many approaches, explanations need evidence, and a problem can have many solutions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name two ways to find out about something, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that there is more than one way to solve a problem.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS3.C: Science and Engineering Use Multiple Approaches to Create New Knowledge and Solve Problems
text: The products of science and engineering are not developed through one set “scientific method” or “engineering design process.” Instead, they use a variety of approaches described in the Science and Engineering Practices. Science explanations are based on a body of evidence and multiple tests, and describe the mechanisms for natural events. Science explanations can change based on new evidence. There is no perfect design in engineering. Designs that are best in some ways (e.g. safety or ease of use) may be inferior in other ways (e.g. cost or aesthetics).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare the approaches used in two investigations and explain why both are scientific.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that science and engineering do not follow one fixed method but use many practices, and explanations rest on evidence.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe two different ways scientists investigate, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name one way scientists investigate.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS3.C: Science and Engineering Use Multiple Approaches to Create New Knowledge and Solve Problems
text: The products of science and engineering are not developed through one set “scientific method” or “engineering design process.” Instead, they use a variety of approaches described in the Science and Engineering Practices. Science explanations are based on a body of evidence and multiple tests, and describe the mechanisms for natural events. Science explanations can change based on new evidence. There is no perfect design in engineering. Designs that are best in some ways (e.g. safety or ease of use) may be inferior in other ways (e.g. cost or aesthetics).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare the approaches used in two investigations and explain why both are scientific.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that science and engineering do not follow one fixed method but use many practices, and explanations rest on evidence.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe two different ways scientists investigate, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name one way scientists investigate.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS3.C: Science and Engineering Use Multiple Approaches to Create New Knowledge and Solve Problems
text: A theory is an explanation of some aspect of the natural world. Scientists develop theories by using multiple approaches. Validity of these theories and explanations is increased through a peer review process that tests and evaluates the evidence supporting scientific claims. Theories are explanations for observable phenomena based on a body of evidence developed over time. A hypothesis is a statement that can be tested to evaluate a theory. Scientific laws describe cause and effect relationships among observable phenomena. Engineers develop solutions using multiple approaches and evaluate their solutions against criteria such as cost, safety, time, and performance. This evaluation often involves trade-offs between constraints to find the optimal solution.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how peer review tested a scientific theory and made it stronger.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that a theory explains part of the natural world, is developed with many approaches, and is strengthened by peer review.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain the difference between a theory and a guess, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what a scientific theory is, with help.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS3.C: Science and Engineering Use Multiple Approaches to Create New Knowledge and Solve Problems
text: Scientists use a variety of methods, tools, and techniques to develop theories. A scientific theory is an explanation of some aspect of the natural word, based on evidence that has been repeatedly confirmed through observation, experimentation (hypothesis-testing), and peer review. The certainty and durability of science findings varies based on the strength of supporting evidence. Theories are usually modified if they are not able to accommodate new evidence. Engineers use a variety of approaches, tools, and techniques to define problems and develop solutions to those problems. Successful engineering solutions meet stakeholder needs and safety requirements, and are economically viable. Trade-offs in design aspects balance competing demands.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the evidence for a scientific theory and explain how multiple methods confirmed it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that scientists use many methods to develop theories, which are explanations based on repeatedly confirmed evidence.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the evidence for one theory, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a scientific theory.
